title: Rule option values are never type-checked: a wrong value crashes the audit at runtime or silently disables the rule
claim: resolveConfig validates option *names* only (`key in rule.defaultOptions`), so a mistyped option value passes config validation and then either throws a TypeError inside auditScreen (every in-app capture, every toBeAccessible() assertion, every `v6y check`) or silently changes what the rule does.
evidence: Probe against packages/core/dist: resolveConfig({rules:{'meaningless-label':['warning',{allow:'OK'}]}}) returns options {allow:'OK'}; audit(...) with that config throws `TypeError: options.allow.some is not a function` (names.ts:78). `touch-target-size: ['error',{minimum:'abc'}]` resolves fine and a 20×20 target produces no issue (visual.ts:43 compares `w < 'abc'`). `text-contrast: ['error',{level:'aaa'}]` resolves and 5.74:1 text passes, while `level:'AAA'` flags it (visual.ts:113 strict-equals 'AAA'). README.md:131 promises "The config is typed and validated" and supports .js/.mjs/.cjs/.json configs where no TypeScript catches this.
impact: A JS/JSON config (or a TS one with a cast) with a wrong-typed option either breaks every audit with a message that does not mention the config, or makes a rule silently stop enforcing (e.g. the 24×24 minimum), which is a wrong result in CI.
fix: In the options loop, check each value against the type of `rule.defaultOptions[key]` (typeof/Array.isArray; for `level` an explicit enum of 'AA'|'AAA') and throw ConfigError(`Rule "${id}" option "${key}" must be ${expected} (got ${JSON.stringify(v)})`). Add tests for a string where an array is expected, a string number, and a lowercase contrast level.

title: `failOn` is not validated: 'none', 'off', 'warn' silently behave like 'error'
claim: Any `failOn` value other than 'never' or 'warning' is treated as 'error' because shouldFail only special-cases those two strings, so plausible spellings change CI behaviour without any error.
evidence: config.ts:182 `failOn: c.failOn ?? 'error'` with no check; engine.ts:157-158 `if (failOn === 'never') return false; return issues.some(i => failOn === 'warning' ? true : i.severity === 'error')`. Probe: shouldFail(errors,{failOn:'none'}) → true, 'off' → true, 'warn' → true, 'errors' → true.
impact: A user writing `failOn: 'none'`/'off' to stop CI failing still gets exit code 1; one writing `failOn: 'warn'` (ESLint habit) expects warnings to fail and gets the weaker error-only gate. Neither gets a message.
fix: Validate in resolveConfig: accept 'error' | 'warning' | 'never' (optionally alias 'warn' → 'warning'), otherwise throw ConfigError listing the choices; make shouldFail exhaustive on the union rather than defaulting to the error path.

title: Unknown top-level/sub keys and wrong-typed non-rule fields are silently ignored despite the README's validation promise
claim: resolveConfig only reads the keys it knows; a typo anywhere outside `rules` (`rule`, `extend`, `screen`, `ignores`, `designsystem`, `hostTypes.txt`) is dropped without a message, and wrong types for `hostTypes.*`/`capture.*` pass through.
evidence: Probe: resolveConfig({rule:{'missing-label':'off'}, extend:'strict', screen:{ignore:['Dev*']}, ignores:['src/**'], designsystem:[...], hostTypes:{txt:['X']}}) returns the plain recommended preset with 0 ignore/screenIgnore/designSystem entries and no error. resolveConfig({hostTypes:{text:'MyText'}}).hostTypes.text === 'MyText' (collect.ts:43 then spreads the string into characters 'M','y','T',…); resolveConfig({capture:{delayMs:'800'}}).capture.delayMs === '800' (used as a setTimeout delay in index.tsx:118). README.md:131: "The config is typed and validated. A typo ... fails with a list of valid choices."
impact: Users (especially with JSON/JS configs or agents writing the config) believe `ignore`/`screens.ignore`/`designSystem` are in effect when they are not; hostTypes as a string silently registers one-letter host names.
fix: Whitelist keys at each level (V6yConfig, screens, hostTypes, capture) and throw ConfigError naming the unknown key and the valid ones; check that ignore/designSystem/screens.ignore/hostTypes.* are string arrays and capture.* are numbers. Add tests.

title: Config `ignore` is applied to the element's source before locations are assigned, so issues reported at an ignored file are not suppressed
claim: suppression() tests `cfg.ignore` against `node.source.file` at issue creation time, but assignLocations later moves the reported `location` to the call site; an issue reported at `src/legacy/Old.tsx:42 via src/components/Button.tsx:9` is therefore not suppressed by `ignore: ['src/legacy/**']`, whereas `ignore: ['src/components/**']` suppresses issues that are reported at app call sites.
evidence: engine.ts:35 computes `suppressed` inside toIssue (before assignLocations at :60); engine.ts:165 uses `node.source!.file`. Probe: auditScreen(DS Button missing-role used from src/legacy/Old.tsx, {designSystem:['src/components/**'], ignore:['src/legacy/**']}) → issues=[{location: src/legacy/Old.tsx:42, via: src/components/Button.tsx:9}], suppressed=0; with ignore:['src/components/**'] instead → issues=0, suppressed=[{by:'config'}]. README.md:122 documents `ignore` as "suppress issues from these source files" with the legacy example; examples/expo-app/v6y.config.ts uses the same pattern.
impact: A legacy screen that uses shared components keeps failing CI despite being ignored, and ignoring a design-system folder hides defects that are reported (and fixable) in app screens.
fix: Move the config-ignore decision after assignLocations/assignScopes and match it against `location` (and `source`, so both the element and the place it is reported at can be ignored); document which files an `ignore` glob covers. Keep inline ignores where they are.

title: Call-site vs component attribution does not match the README and is inconsistent at 2 call sites
claim: README says shared-component issues move to the call site once 3+ call sites share them, but assignScopes overrides that: when every rendered use has the issue and there are ≥2 immediate callers, the issue is reported at the component (`scope:'component'`, location reset to source, `via` deleted) even with 3+ callers or with `designSystem`; and when 2 callers exist and only one has the issue, the issue is marked `scope:'call-site'` while `location` stays the component file with no `via`.
evidence: engine.ts:140 `uniform = nodes === rendered && sites.length >= 2`; :142-146 set scope component, `i.location = i.source`, `delete i.via`; :147-149 otherwise set 'call-site' without touching location (assignLocations only moved it at ≥3 sites, :101). Probes: 3 uses all missing a role → all three `scope:'component', location: src/Button.tsx:9, callSites:[1,2,3]`; 2 uses, one bad → `scope:'call-site', location: src/Button.tsx:9, via: undefined` (groupIssues lists A.tsx:1 as usedAt); designSystem + 2 uses both missing a label → `scope:'component'` at IconButton.tsx:9. README.md:144 describes only the call-site move ("automatically once the same issue comes from 3 or more call sites") and never mentions component scope.
impact: Users and the GitHub annotation step expect the diff line in their screen to be annotated; instead the common design-system case (every use broken) lands on the component file, and a 'call-site' issue can point at a file that is not the call site. The README is wrong about the behaviour users will actually see.
fix: Document component scope (and `callSites`) in the README's shared-components section. Make the thresholds coherent: use one constant for "shared component" (≥2 callers), move non-uniform issues to the call site via `via` whenever the component has ≥2 callers, and never set `scope:'call-site'` while `location` points at the component. Add a test for the 2-site non-uniform case.

title: nested-interactive can be blamed on the inner shared component ("fix it once") although the defect is the caller's nesting
claim: CALLER_RULES only exempts duplicate-label, but nested-interactive is also a context rule (the fix is on the enclosing pressable at the call site); when a shared control is used from ≥2 places that are all inside pressables, assignScopes marks the issue `scope:'component'` at the inner component with the callers listed, and the CLI prints "inside this shared component; fix it once".
evidence: engine.ts:74 `CALLER_RULES = new Set(['duplicate-label'])`; roles.ts:39-49 nested-interactive derives entirely from ctx.ancestors. Probe: two Feed.tsx pressables each wrapping an IconButton (source src/components/IconButton.tsx:9) → both issues `scope:'component', location: src/components/IconButton.tsx:9, callSites:[Feed.tsx:11, Feed.tsx:31]`, with and without designSystem. cli/src/format.ts:55 prints the "fix it once" line for scope 'component'.
impact: The report sends the developer to a component that is fine and tells them to fix it there; the real fix (`accessible={false}` on the outer element or restructuring) is at the call sites. GitHub annotations land on the wrong file.
fix: Add 'nested-interactive' to CALLER_RULES (its node is the inner element, but the fix is the caller's). Consider letting rules declare `scope: 'call-site'` in Finding (tri-state) so text-contrast can do the same when the failing background layer comes from outside the component. Add a test mirroring the probe.

title: Setting `designSystem` disables the automatic call-site heuristic for every component outside the globs
claim: assignLocations uses `if (cfg.designSystem.length) {...} else if (auto)`, so once any designSystem glob is configured, a shared component that the globs miss is never moved to its call sites even with 3+ callers; the README presents designSystem as making the automatic behaviour explicit, not as replacing it.
evidence: engine.ts:99-103. Probe: src/alf/Button.tsx used from 3 sites with one good use → without designSystem the 3 issues are at src/A.tsx:1/2/3 via Button; with designSystem:['src/components/**'] they stay at src/alf/Button.tsx:9 with no via. README.md:144 "Name your shared components with `designSystem` to make it explicit." REPORT-v2 shows Bluesky needed four globs to cover its shared code.
impact: Adding a partial designSystem list silently makes attribution worse for everything it does not list.
fix: Apply the 3-site heuristic to sources that are not in designSystem as well (designSystem adds certainty, auto mode remains the fallback), or state in the README that designSystem replaces the automatic mode.

title: `uniform` counts every host node carrying a source line, so wrappers around library components that render sibling hosts never reach component scope
claim: assignScopes compares the number of nodes with the issue to the number of all visible nodes whose `source` is that line; a stamped element that yields several host nodes (a node_modules component rendering a fragment of hosts, which collect.ts gives the same source) or nodes the rule cannot apply to makes `nodes === rendered` false, so an identical defect is reported per call site for one component and once at the component for another.
evidence: engine.ts:124-125 builds `rendered` from every visible node with a source; :139-140 compares. collect.ts:330-335 gives every host under an unstamped composite the innermost stamped source. Probe Q1: 3 uses of Button.tsx:9 where each use yields a View and a sibling Text with the same source → missing-role is `scope:'call-site'` at Home.tsx:1/2/3 via Button; the same tree with the Text stamped separately (Button.tsx:12) → `scope:'component'` at Button.tsx:9 with callSites [1,2,3].
impact: Attribution depends on an implementation detail of the wrapped library rather than on the defect; the "fix it once" report is missed for exactly the wrappers it was designed for.
fix: Count rendered nodes per (source, type) or, better, only nodes the rule evaluated (have each `check` call recorded per rule so uniform = issues / evaluated candidates for that rule and source).

title: Option-name validation uses `in`, so inherited Object.prototype keys pass
claim: `key in rule.defaultOptions` is true for `toString`, `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty` and `__proto__`, so those keys are accepted as rule options and merged into the resolved options.
evidence: Probe: resolveConfig({rules:{'touch-target-size':['error',{toString:1}]}}) → options include toString:1; `['error',{constructor:1}]` on missing-label (which "takes no options") → {constructor:1}; a JSON config with "__proto__" passes (spread creates an own property, so no prototype pollution, but no error either).
impact: Validation is weaker than advertised; a no-options rule accepts an object with these keys.
fix: Use `Object.hasOwn(rule.defaultOptions, key)` (or Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call).

title: Level vocabulary is inconsistent across config, CLI, docs and README ('warning' vs 'warn' vs '—')
claim: The config rejects ESLint's 'warn' although V6yConfig.rules is documented as "ESLint-style", while `v6y rules` and the README table print 'warn' and '—' and docs/rules print 'warning' and 'off', so the word a user copies from one surface is invalid in another.
evidence: config.ts:125 LEVELS = ['off','warning','error']; config.ts:13 doc comment "ESLint-style"; probe: `'missing-label': 'warn'` → ConfigError. cli/src/index.ts:273-275 prints 'warn'/'—'; README.md:170-181 uses 'warn'/'—'; docs.ts:16 and docs/rules/README.md print 'warning'/'off'.
impact: Minor friction and support questions; agents generating configs from the table will produce invalid levels.
fix: Accept 'warn' as an alias normalised to 'warning' (keep the error for anything else), and use one vocabulary ('error' | 'warning' | 'off') in formatRules, the README table and docs.

title: Glob semantics are undocumented and surprising for screen names (`*` never matches `/`; braces and `./` are literal)
claim: globToRegExp makes `*` match `[^/]*`, which is right for files but means `screens.ignore: ['(tabs)*']` does not match Expo Router's `(tabs)/index` and `Dev*` does not match `Dev/Menu`; `{a,b}` alternation, `!` negation and a leading `./` are treated as literal characters without any warning.
evidence: Probe: '(tabs)*' vs '(tabs)/index' → false; '(tabs)/**' → true; 'Dev*' vs 'Dev/Menu' → false; './src/**' vs 'src/a.ts' → false; 'src/{a,b}/**' vs 'src/a/x.ts' → false (regex /^src\/\{a,b\}\/.*$/). README.md:19/122-123 and config.ts:16-19 only show `src/legacy/**` and `Storybook*`.
impact: Expo Router users (route names contain `/`) write an ignore that silently does nothing; brace globs copied from other tools silently never match.
fix: Document the supported subset (`**`, `*`, `?`, no braces/negation, paths relative to the project root). For screen names, consider letting `*` match `/` since route names are not paths, or document `**`. Optionally throw a ConfigError on `{`, `!` or a leading `./`.

title: Rule options are sticky across preset/rule layers, which the config doc does not say
claim: Options accumulate in `optionLayers` independently of the level, so a later layer that sets only a level keeps earlier options (ESLint semantics), while V6yConfig.extends is documented as "Later entries and `rules` override earlier ones".
evidence: config.ts:152-164 merges options into optionLayers and only sets `level`; :167-169 applies the accumulated options. Probe: extends:['wcag22-aa','recommended'] → touch-target-size options {platformGuidelines:false,...}; extends:'wcag22-aa' + rules {'touch-target-size':'error'} → still platformGuidelines:false.
impact: A user who re-sets a rule to 'error' expecting defaults keeps the preset's options and gets different findings than they expect.
fix: Document the behaviour in the `extends`/`rules` doc comments and README ("a bare level keeps options from earlier layers; pass `[level, {}]`… " or reset to defaults), and add a test that pins whichever semantics are chosen.

title: WCAG 2.5.5 and `WcagCriterion.since` are defined but unused, while the 44pt advisory finding cites 2.5.8
claim: The advisory 'below the Apple HIG / Material recommendation' finding inherits `wcag: ['2.5.8']` (24×24 minimum) although it is not a 2.5.8 failure, whereas `WCAG['2.5.5']` (Target Size Enhanced, 44×44, AAA) exists in wcag.ts and is referenced by no rule; `since` is never read anywhere.
evidence: visual.ts:51-58 advisory finding has no `wcag` override; engine.ts:28 `wcag: f.wcag ?? wcag`. Probe: a 30×30 target → {severity:'warning', wcag:['2.5.8'], message:'...below the Apple HIG recommendation of 44×44'}. grep: '2.5.5' appears only in wcag.ts:20/34; `since` only in wcag.ts.
impact: Reports and GitHub annotations label a platform-guideline warning as a WCAG 2.5.8 issue, which overstates it for compliance tracking.
fix: Set `wcag: ['2.5.5']` on the advisory finding (it is exactly the AAA 44×44 criterion) and either show `since` in the generated docs ("WCAG 2.2") or remove the field.

title: `wcag21aa` re-sets 'missing-role' to 'error' although it already spreads `strict`
claim: The explicit `'missing-role': 'error'` in the wcag21-aa preset is redundant with `...strict`, which already sets it to 'error'.
evidence: config.ts:68-74 strict sets 'missing-role': 'error'; config.ts:81-86 `const wcag21aa = { ...strict, 'missing-role': 'error', 'touch-target-size': 'off' }`.
impact: Noise that suggests the two presets differ on missing-role when they do not.
fix: Remove the line (or, if the intent was to keep it an error even if strict changes, add a comment saying so).

title: Snapshot fields the collector fills but no rule or engine code reads (hint, style.opacity, window.fontScale, InlineIgnore.source)
claim: `A11yNode.hint`, `NodeStyle.opacity`, `ScreenSnapshot.window` (incl. fontScale) and `InlineIgnore.source` are populated by collect.ts/index.tsx but never consumed; in particular text-contrast ignores `opacity`, so semi-transparent text is scored at full opacity. `Issue.wcag`'s doc says "WCAG 2.1 success criteria" while 2.5.8 is 2.2.
evidence: grep across packages/*/src: `.hint` only written at collect.ts:304; `opacity` only at types.ts:49 and collect.ts:98; `fontScale`/`window` only at index.tsx:146 and types.ts:117; `ignore[].source` only set at collect.ts:339 and asserted in collect.test.tsx:115; tree.ts effectiveTextColor/effectiveBackground never read opacity. types.ts:128 comment.
impact: Dead weight in every snapshot and a mild wrong result for faded text; readers of types.ts assume these influence audits.
fix: Either use them (apply `opacity` when compositing fg/bg in tree.ts; use `window` to skip off-screen frames; show `hint` in messages) or drop them from the snapshot format and mark the rest as informational in the doc comments; change the Issue.wcag comment to "WCAG 2.x".

title: Two host-type tables have drifted, and `hostTypes` config is applied only at capture time, never by the engine
claim: tree.ts keeps its own TEXT/INPUT/IMAGE tables as a fallback when `kind` is absent (`AndroidText` exists only there), while collect.ts BUILTIN_KINDS is the table that config `hostTypes` extends; engine.ts never reads `cfg.hostTypes`, so re-auditing saved snapshots (`v6y check`, Metro's readReport) with a changed `hostTypes` has no effect until screens are re-captured.
evidence: tree.ts:4-9 vs collect.ts:30-36; grep for hostTypes: only config.ts:176-179 (resolve), index.tsx:138 and jest.ts:94 (passed to collect). engine.ts has no reference. README.md:127 presents `hostTypes` as ordinary config.
impact: Editing `hostTypes` and running `v6y check` on existing snapshots silently does nothing; two lists to keep in sync.
fix: Export one `BUILTIN_KINDS` table from core (tree.ts) and have collect.ts import it; in the engine, when `node.kind` is undefined, classify `node.type` with `cfg.hostTypes` as well (or document that hostTypes needs a re-capture).

title: `export *` of every module makes internals public, and `defineRule` is exported although custom rules cannot be registered
claim: The `v6y` package's main entry re-exports tree/color/docs/examples helpers (effectiveBackground, blend, toHex, RULE_EXAMPLES, OPTION_DOCS, renderRulesIndex, …) as public API, and exports `defineRule`/`Rule` while `RuleId` is a closed union, resolveConfig throws on unknown rule ids and the engine only iterates `rulesById`, so a user who finds `defineRule` has no way to use it.
evidence: index.ts:1-9; node -e listing of dist exports (53 names incl. effectiveFontWeight, suggestTextColor, DOCS_BASE); rules/index.ts:42 `RuleId = keyof RuleOptionsMap`; config.ts:144-147 unknown rule → ConfigError; engine.ts:19 `rulesById[id as RuleId]`. packages/v6y/package.json main → dist/core/index.js.
impact: Every helper becomes a compatibility commitment for a tool meant to be widely adopted, and the API suggests extensibility that does not exist.
fix: Curate index.ts (types, defineConfig, presets, resolveConfig, audit/auditScreen/shouldFail/groupIssues, allRules/rulesById, docs renderers, ruleDocsUrl), keep helpers under a subpath or namespace; either add a `plugins: Rule[]` config path (RulesConfig keyed by string for plugin ids) or stop exporting defineRule.

title: Generated 'Configure' sample uses 'error' and a no-op default option, contradicting the heuristic note above it
claim: renderRuleDoc builds the sample from the first option and its default (`['error', { allow: [] }]`), so heuristic rules show an 'error' configuration two sections after the page says they are warnings in every preset, and the option shown changes nothing.
evidence: docs.ts:55 `const sample = options.length ? `['error', { ${options[0][0]}: ${JSON.stringify(options[0][1])} }]` : `'warning'``; probe output for meaningless-label: `rules: { 'meaningless-label': ['error', { allow: [] }] }`; docs.ts:36 prints the heuristic sentence; docs/rules/meaningless-label.md shows both.
impact: Users copy a config that does nothing useful; the page contradicts itself.
fix: Use the rule's strict-preset level and an illustrative value (e.g. keep a `sample` field in OPTION_DOCS or RULE_EXAMPLES per rule), or drop options from the sample and link to the options table.

title: README rule table is hand-maintained and untested, unlike docs/rules
claim: docs.test.ts fails when docs/rules drifts from the rules, but the README table (levels, WCAG, options) is maintained by hand with a different vocabulary and no test, so it will drift the next time a preset or option changes.
evidence: docs.test.ts:16-21 checks only docs/rules; README.md:168-181 is static text (currently consistent with presets, checked by hand); scripts/gen-docs.mjs writes only docs/rules.
impact: Drift between README and behaviour is the kind of inconsistency this audit is about; it is only a matter of time.
fix: Generate the README table from renderRulesIndex() between markers in gen-docs.mjs, or add a test that compares the README rows to presets/OPTION_DOCS.

title: resolveConfig(null) throws a TypeError instead of a ConfigError
claim: A config that is `null` (a v6y.config.json containing `null`, or a JS module whose default export is null) reaches `(config as ResolvedConfig).resolved` and throws `Cannot read properties of null`, bypassing the helpful-error path.
evidence: Probe: resolveConfig(null) → TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'resolved'). cli/src/index.ts:41 `config = JSON.parse(...)` then :64 resolveConfig(config) with no null check (jest.ts:47 does `?? {}`).
impact: An unhelpful crash instead of "config must be an object".
fix: Guard: if config is null/non-object throw ConfigError('v6y config must export an object'); default `config ?? {}`.

title: Suppressed issues still count towards component scope and appear in callSites
claim: assignScopes runs over all issues including suppressed ones, so a use the developer explicitly silenced with v6y-ignore both makes the group 'uniform' and is listed under "Used at" for the component-scope issue.
evidence: engine.ts:61 `assignScopes(all, visible)` with `all` containing suppressed issues; :138 sites from the whole group. Probe: 2 uses, the second inline-ignored → remaining issue `scope:'component', callSites:[1,2]`, suppressed=1.
impact: The report tells the developer to fix the component once and lists a call site they already judged fine; minor but contradicts the suppression.
fix: Compute uniform/callSites over unsuppressed issues only (or document that ignores do not affect attribution).

title: Every Issue carries the full ownerSources chain (up to 16 locations) into reports and JSON output
claim: toIssue copies `node.ownerSources` onto each Issue; it is only needed internally by assignLocations/assignScopes/groupIssues, yet it is serialised in SnapshotReport, `v6y check --format json` and saved reports, ~1.2 KB per issue with deep chains.
evidence: engine.ts:33; collect.ts:26 MAX_OWNER_SOURCES = 16; probe: an issue with 16 owners serialises to 1194 bytes with keys [... 'ownerSources' ...]; cli/src/index.ts:186 prints a.issues as JSON; mcp.ts:131-140 already strips it for structuredContent.
impact: Noisy JSON for consumers and a public field whose meaning overlaps with `callSites`/`via`/`location`.
fix: Keep ownerSources on an internal working type and strip it from the public Issue after scoping (callSites/via/location carry what consumers need), or document it as the raw caller chain.

title: Install instructions point at an npm package that does not exist, and nothing says so
claim: README ("Setup: one line", `npm i -D v6y`), docs/agents.md:5, the Claude Code plugin's `npx --no-install v6y mcp` (.mcp.json) and action.yml:38 all assume `v6y` is on npm, but `npm view v6y` returns E404 and no document states the package is unpublished or how to try it from the repo.
evidence: Ran `npm view v6y name version` from the repo: "404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/v6y". Grepped README.md, docs/, integrations/, action.yml for 'publish'/'not yet'/'unpublished': no hits. README:258 even lists "a single `v6y` npm package" under "Next up", although packages/v6y exists (commit cd102a4 "Ship as one package") and only publishing is missing. examples/expo-app/package.json:38 uses `"v6y": "file:../../packages/v6y"`, the only working install path, and only the example README hints at it.
impact: The first command every reader runs fails; the agents story (plugin, Codex, Cursor) and the GitHub Action are equally dead for anyone outside this monorepo. Readers cannot tell whether they did something wrong.
fix: Add a short 'Status: not on npm yet' note at the top of README (and docs/agents.md) with the working path today: clone, `npm install && npm run build`, then `"v6y": "file:../v6y/packages/v6y"` or `npm pack packages/v6y`. Replace the 'single npm package' bullet in Next up with 'publish to npm'. Remove the note once published (the name is free).

title: 'Status and known gaps' contradicts the commit history and the example README about device testing
claim: README says the runtime is 'Not yet verified … on a real simulator or device, in particular measureInWindow and screen-change detection under the new architecture' and lists 'run on a simulator' as next up, but commit 86e9c23 records a real-device run (Android, Expo Go, new architecture, with fixes to SourceCode.getConstants(), focused-screen detection and first-capture timing) and examples/expo-app/README.md:54,64 describes device-only behaviour (tab-bar contrast reported against `(tabs)/_layout.tsx`).
evidence: `git show 86e9c23` message: "Field-tested on a real device and on Bluesky's app … Device (Android, Expo Go, new architecture): read the dev server URL via SourceCode.getConstants() (bridgeless); tab-bar buttons are no longer mistaken for the focused screen; wait for navigation before the first capture". That commit's README diff touches no line containing 'verif', 'device' or 'simulator' (grep on `git show 86e9c23 -- README.md`). The v6y-field reports (REPORT.md, REPORT-v2.md, LOOP-LOG.md) are Jest-only, so the device run is recorded nowhere but the commit.
impact: Readers either distrust a tool whose own README says it was never run on a device, or (worse) assume iOS/Fabric was covered when only Android/Expo Go was. The 'Next up' list is also stale (simulator, single package).
fix: Rewrite the section from facts: tested on Android (Expo Go, new architecture) on <date>; not yet on iOS, on a bare RN (non-Expo) app, or with Paper; what was observed (measureInWindow frames, route tracking). Keep 'Next up' to things that are actually next (npm publish, iOS run, overlay, Maestro/Detox, 200% font scale).

title: The 'Without Metro integration' path does not work as documented: wrong report endpoint and v6y.config.ts not applied
claim: README says: add `v6y/babel`, `import 'v6y/auto'`, run `npx v6y dev`. But the app posts reports to the Metro origin from the bundle URL (`<scriptURL origin>/v6y/report`, i.e. port 8081) unless `configure({}, { endpoint })` is called, while `v6y dev` listens on 8973; and without `withV6y`, `v6y/project-config` is the empty default so the in-app audit runs with the `recommended` preset regardless of v6y.config.ts, and `v6y dev` prints the app's issues as-is (it only re-audits when a report has no `issues`).
evidence: packages/react-native/src/index.tsx:65-72 `devServerEndpoint()` returns `${origin ?? 'http://localhost:8081'}/v6y/report` unless `runtime.endpoint` is set; index.tsx:161-171 `send()` swallows failures. packages/cli/src/index.ts:25 `DEFAULT_PORT = 8973`; index.ts:258 prints the needed `configure({}, { endpoint: … })` hint only at runtime. packages/react-native/src/auto.ts:5-10 and :15-16: `require('@v6y/react-native/project-config')` is the empty module without Metro ('minus the project config'). index.ts:224 `if (Array.isArray(data.issues)) return resolve(data)`. README never mentions `configure`, `endpoint`, or that the config is not loaded on this path.
impact: A user on a custom bundler or without withV6y follows the README, sees nothing in the `v6y dev` terminal (the POSTs go to Metro and fail silently), and any in-app summary uses the wrong rules. Nothing tells them why.
fix: Document the path fully: `import { configure } from 'v6y/react-native'; configure(require('./v6y.config').default, { endpoint: 'http://<host>:8973/v6y/report' })` before `import 'v6y/auto'`, or make `v6y dev` the default endpoint when the Metro POST fails (try 8081 then 8973), and have `v6y dev` re-audit every report with the project config instead of trusting `issues`. Also mention `adb reverse` is done for you.

title: `v6y init` always writes a TypeScript config that Node < 22.18 cannot load, and the Metro report receiver is affected too, not only 'the CLI'
claim: `init` writes `v6y.config.ts` without checking the Node version; `loadConfig` needs Node ≥ 22.18 for `.ts`, and `withV6y`'s middleware calls `loadConfig(projectRoot)` before reading each report, so on Node 20/22.0–22.17 every screen capture ends in a 400 and `[v6y] v6y.config.ts: loading TypeScript configs needs Node 22.18 or newer…` in the Metro terminal. README:131 says the requirement applies only 'when loaded by the CLI', and no package declares `engines`.
evidence: index.ts:305-311 writes `v6y.config.ts` unconditionally (reproduced in the scratchpad: 'Created v6y.config.ts'). index.ts:35,58-59 the Node ≥ 22.18 error. packages/metro/src/index.ts:132 `const report = await readReport(req, await loadConfig(projectRoot));` evaluates `loadConfig` first, so it throws before `readReport`, caught at :136-139 (console.error + 400). `grep -rn engines package.json packages/*/package.json` → nothing. Jest (packages/react-native/src/jest.ts:46 `require(file)`) and the Metro bundle are unaffected, which makes the failure confusing: tests pass, the app audits, only the terminal reports fail.
impact: The 'one line setup' produces a broken first run for anyone on Node 20 or an early 22.x; the error is actionable but the user had no chance to avoid it.
fix: In `init`, write `v6y.config.js` with `// @ts-check` and `/** @type {import('v6y').V6yConfig} */` when `process.versions.node` < 22.18 (or always, and offer `--ts`). Add `engines: { node: '>=20' }` (and the 22.18 note for `.ts`) to packages/v6y/package.json, and change README:131 to say the requirement applies to the CLI and the Metro dev server.

title: 'Kept … for compliance reports' overclaims: suppressed issues and their reasons are never surfaced by any command
claim: README says the `-- reason` after a `v6y-ignore` 'is kept with suppressed issues for compliance reports', but `v6y check` prints only a count ('N suppressed by v6y-ignore comments or config.'), `--format json` emits only `a.issues`, and the GitHub format ignores suppressed issues; there is no report that lists suppressions or reasons.
evidence: packages/cli/src/index.ts:163 `if (a.suppressed) out.push(dim(`${a.suppressed} suppressed …`))` (a number, not the issues); index.ts:181-182 `console.log(JSON.stringify(a.issues, null, 2))`; `Analysis.suppressed` is a `number` (index.ts:112). `grep -rni complian README.md docs packages/*/src` matches only README:162. The reason exists only in the engine result (`Issue.suppressed.reason`, types.ts:152) and the in-app SnapshotReport.
impact: Teams adopting v6y for EAA/ADA work expect an audit trail of what was silenced and why; the README promises one that does not exist.
fix: Either add it (`v6y check --format json` → `{ issues, suppressed }`, and a `--suppressed` flag for the text report listing file:line, rule, by, reason) or reword to 'kept in the audit result (`suppressed[].suppressed.reason`) so tooling can report on it'.

title: Legal-standard framing (EU Accessibility Act, ADA Title II) with no scope statement in the README
claim: The presets table sells `wcag21-aa` as 'the standard behind the EU Accessibility Act … and US ADA Title II' (repeated in the init template and example config) while the README never says that v6y's 12 rules cover about 8 of WCAG 2.1 AA's 50 success criteria and that a passing check is not conformance; the only disclaimers are in the generated docs/rules/README.md:22 and the Claude skill (SKILL.md:29).
evidence: README.md:139-140; packages/cli/src/index.ts:293 init template comment '(EU Accessibility Act, ADA Title II)'; examples/expo-app/v6y.config.ts:5-6. Rule WCAG coverage from `allRules` meta: 4.1.2, 2.4.6, 1.1.1, 3.3.2, 1.3.1, 2.5.8, 1.4.3, 1.4.4 (plus 1.4.6 at AAA). `grep -c 'VoiceOver\|TalkBack\|not all\|conformance' README.md` → 0.
impact: Readers and their legal/compliance stakeholders may treat 'passes wcag21-aa' as evidence of conformance; that is the kind of claim that damages trust once noticed.
fix: Add one paragraph under Presets (and in Status): 'v6y checks the criteria that can be derived from the component tree (list them). It does not check focus order, announcements, gestures, timing, media, or anything requiring a person; a clean report is a necessary start, not conformance. Test key flows with VoiceOver and TalkBack.' Rename the row text to 'the WCAG 2.1 AA criteria v6y can check'.

title: `v6y check` / `v6y fix` die with a raw ENOENT when no snapshots exist or the glob matches nothing
claim: The CLI reads each positional argument with `fs.readFileSync`, so a first run before any snapshot was recorded (bash passes the literal `.v6y/snapshots/*.json`) prints `v6y: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.v6y/snapshots/*.json'` and exits 2, while the MCP server already has the helpful message and expands globs itself.
evidence: Reproduced: `node packages/v6y/dist/cli/bin.js check '.v6y/snapshots/*.json'` → "v6y: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.v6y/snapshots/*.json'", exit 2. index.ts:125-126 `for (const f of files) { const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'))`. packages/cli/src/mcp.ts:75-99 `expandGlob` and :115-118 'No v6y snapshots match …. Record some first: run the tests with V6Y_SNAPSHOTS=… or open the screens in the app running with withV6y().'
impact: The most likely first error a new user hits (nothing recorded yet, or zsh/CI quoting) is a Node error with no hint about V6Y_SNAPSHOTS or withV6y.
fix: In bin.ts expand positional patterns with `expandGlob` (move it to index.ts), and when nothing matches print the MCP message and exit 2; default to `.v6y/snapshots/*.json` when no positional is given instead of erroring.

title: `v6y init`'s 'Last step' snippet is incomplete for Expo apps and init does nothing about .gitignore or Jest
claim: When no metro.config.js exists (the default for Expo projects), init prints only the two `withV6y` lines; `getDefaultConfig` is undefined in that snippet, the user is not told to create the file, and init neither adds `.v6y/` to .gitignore nor mentions `setupFilesAfterEnv: ['v6y/jest']`.
evidence: Reproduced in an empty scratchpad dir: output is 'Created v6y.config.ts / Last step: wrap your Metro config in metro.config.js: / const { withV6y } = require('v6y/metro'); / module.exports = withV6y(getDefaultConfig(__dirname));'. index.ts:312-318: the `getDefaultConfig` require line is never printed; no .gitignore or Jest handling anywhere in `init`.
impact: The 'one line' onboarding stalls at the first step for Expo users (ReferenceError: getDefaultConfig is not defined) and later surprises them with a committed .v6y/ directory.
fix: Print the complete three-line file (`const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config'); // or '@react-native/metro-config'`), detect Expo via package.json and offer to write metro.config.js (or say `npx expo customize metro.config.js`), append `.v6y/` to .gitignore when absent, and print the Jest line as an optional next step.

title: Nothing tells users to ignore `.v6y/` in git although the Metro middleware writes a snapshot file on every screen visit
claim: README:41 says reports are saved to `.v6y/snapshots/` and the CI section regenerates them from tests, but no document says whether to commit them or to add `.v6y/` to .gitignore; the repo and the example both ignore it, so the maintainers' intent is 'do not commit'.
evidence: `grep -c gitignore README.md docs/agents.md examples/expo-app/README.md` → 0 everywhere. .gitignore:4 and examples/expo-app/.gitignore:44 contain `.v6y/`. packages/cli/src/index.ts:201-206 writes `<screen>.<platform>.json` per report; example snapshots are 14–159 KB each (ls -la examples/expo-app/.v6y/snapshots).
impact: Users commit large, machine-specific JSON (absolute-time `capturedAt`, device window sizes) that churns on every run and makes `--changed` staleness checks meaningless in CI.
fix: Add one line to README Setup ('add `.v6y/` to .gitignore; CI records fresh snapshots from your tests') and let `init` do it.

title: No supported-versions matrix or `engines`: Node, React, React Native, Expo, architecture and platforms are undocumented
claim: The README never states which Node, React, React Native or Expo versions are supported, whether old/new architecture, Expo Go vs dev builds, iOS vs Android, or Windows; the only machine-readable hint is `peerDependencies: react >=18, react-native >=0.72` (both optional), which nothing in the repo tests (the example is RN 0.88 / React 19.3; root devDependencies are React 18.3).
evidence: packages/v6y/package.json:14-15; no `engines` in any package.json (grep). README mentions 'Node' twice (only the 22.18 note), 'new architecture' once (as unverified), 'Expo Go' 0 times. packages/react-native/src/collect.ts:11 comment 'React work tags (stable across React 17–19)'. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs only Node 24.
impact: Adopters cannot tell whether their stack is supported before trying; bug reports will be noise about unsupported versions.
fix: Add a 'Requirements' section (Node ≥ 20, ≥ 22.18 for .ts config; React 18–19; RN ≥ 0.7x actually tested; Expo SDK 5x; Paper/Fabric; iOS/Android; Expo Go/dev builds; macOS/Linux) and matching `engines`, and a CI matrix for at least two Node versions.

title: No 'how it works' overview or FAQ; 'snapshot' is used before it is ever defined
claim: The pipeline (Babel stamps `__v6y` file:line props → fiber walk → JSON snapshot → rules → report; snapshots recorded by the app via Metro or by `toBeAccessible()` with V6Y_SNAPSHOTS; `check`/`fix` re-audit saved snapshots, which is why line numbers go stale) is scattered over README:37-41, 185, 215 and code comments; 'snapshots' first appears at README:41 with no definition, and there is no FAQ on false positives, heuristic rules, or when to use `v6y-ignore` vs `ignore` vs `screens.ignore` vs rule options like `includeRepeated`.
evidence: README headings: Setup, In your tests, Fix automatically, With coding agents, Configuration, Rules, CI and pre-commit, What's in the package, Development, Status. The word 'heuristic' appears in README only in the presets table; the heuristic note exists only in generated pages (packages/core/src/docs.ts:36). The clearest end-to-end description is in packages/core/src/types.ts:1-6 and packages/metro/src/index.ts:1-15.
impact: Readers cannot predict what v6y can and cannot see (styles-only contrast, no layout in Jest, no native nav bars), so they misread results as false positives or miss real limitations.
fix: Add a short 'How it works' section (five bullets and the three ways a snapshot is produced) and a FAQ: 'I think this is a false positive', 'why is the issue reported via a component', 'why no touch-target issues in Jest', 'which ignore to use', 'what to do when a snapshot is stale'.

title: Vitest is advertised but the matcher only self-registers under Jest-style globals, and types target `namespace jest`
claim: README:227 and the module header say `v6y/jest` works 'for Jest and Vitest', but registration is `globalThis.expect?.extend(matchers)` at import time; with Vitest's default `globals: false` nothing registers and `expect(x).toBeAccessible is not a function` appears with no hint, the exported `matchers` for a manual `expect.extend` is undocumented, and the type augmentation is only `declare global { namespace jest … }`.
evidence: jest.ts:154-155 `const globalExpect = (globalThis as any).expect; if (globalExpect?.extend) globalExpect.extend(matchers);`; jest.ts:141 `export const matchers`; jest.ts:143-151 Jest-only types. No Vitest example in README, docs/agents.md or examples/. `grep -c globals README.md` → 0.
impact: Vitest users (common with Expo web/RN-web and monorepos) get a silent no-op from the documented setup.
fix: Document the Vitest form: `import { expect } from 'vitest'; import { matchers } from 'v6y/jest'; expect.extend(matchers);` plus a `declare module 'vitest' { interface Assertion<T> { toBeAccessible … } }` augmentation shipped in jest.d.ts; optionally fall back to `require('vitest').expect` when the global is missing.

title: The Claude Code commit gate silently lets commits through when `v6y check` errors out
claim: The hook blocks only on exit status 1 (accessibility errors); when `v6y check` exits 2 (invalid config, TypeScript config on Node < 22.18, unreadable snapshot, `--changed needs a git repository`) it exits 0 with no output, so the gate described in docs/agents.md:28-30 ('If there are errors, the commit is blocked') disappears without anyone noticing.
evidence: pre-commit-check.mjs:27-35: `if (result.status === 1) { … process.exit(2); } process.exit(0);` with no branch for status 2 or spawn failure; packages/cli/src/bin.ts:91-94 maps any thrown error to exit 2, and index.ts:59-61 throws for config problems.
impact: Teams relying on the gate get no protection exactly when their setup broke, and get no message pointing at the broken config.
fix: On status 2 (or a spawn error) write `v6y could not run the commit check: <stderr>` to stdout/stderr and either exit 2 or exit 0 with a visible warning (hook JSON `systemMessage`); mention this behaviour in docs/agents.md.

title: Missing open-source essentials: CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, templates, license section, versioning policy, release process
claim: The repo has LICENSE and a CI workflow but no CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (build/test/`npm run docs` requirement), CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE or PR template; README has no License or Contributing section; README says 'pre-alpha' while packages/v6y and the plugin are versioned 0.1.0, there are no git tags, and no statement of what 0.x versions promise.
evidence: `ls CHANGELOG* CONTRIBUTING* CODE_OF_CONDUCT* SECURITY*` → none; `find .github -type f` → only workflows/ci.yml; `git tag` → empty; README.md:241 'This is pre-alpha'; packages/v6y/package.json:3 '0.1.0'; integrations/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3 '0.1.0'. packages/core/test/docs.test.ts:16-21 fails when docs/rules is stale, which a contributor only learns from the test name.
impact: Contributors do not know how to build, regenerate docs or report issues; users cannot tell what changed between runs or how stable the config format is, which matters for a tool meant to be adopted as a standard.
fix: Add CONTRIBUTING.md (npm install, npm test, `npm run docs` after touching rules, how to add a rule with example + option docs), CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog, start at 0.1.0), issue templates (bug with snapshot attached, false positive, new rule), SECURITY.md, a README License section, and a one-line versioning policy (0.x: config and snapshot format may change; rules added as minor).

title: 'What's in the package' table omits the `fix` and `mcp` commands
claim: The entry-point table says `npx v6y` provides 'the `init`, `rules`, `check` and `dev` commands', but the CLI also has `fix` and `mcp`, both headline features documented elsewhere in the same README.
evidence: packages/cli/src/bin.ts:39-56 (`case 'fix'`, `case 'mcp'`) and HELP at bin.ts:17-19; README.md:75-107 documents both; README.md:228 lists four commands.
impact: A reader skimming the package overview misses two of the main reasons to install.
fix: Update the row to 'init, rules, check, fix, dev and mcp' (or link to the help text).

title: No `--version` flag; `v6y --version` prints 'Unknown command' and exits 2
claim: The CLI has no `--version`/`-v`, so the standard first thing people type (and what bug reports ask for) fails with the full help text and a non-zero exit.
evidence: Reproduced: `node packages/v6y/dist/cli/bin.js --version` → 'Unknown command: --version' + help, exit 2. bin.ts:75-84 handles only `help`, `--help`, `-h`. The version is already read for `mcp` at bin.ts:53 via `require('../package.json')`.
impact: Minor friction; bug reports will lack the version.
fix: Add `case '--version': case '-v': console.log(version); return 0;` and list it in HELP.

title: The README copied into the npm package carries relative links that will be broken on npmjs.com
claim: The build copies the repo README verbatim into packages/v6y, but README links `./examples/expo-app` (README:18), `./docs/agents.md` (:107) and `./docs/rules/README.md` (:166) point at directories that are not in the package `files`, so they 404 on the npm page once published.
evidence: bundle.mjs:81-82 `fs.copyFileSync(path.join(packages, '..', 'README.md'), path.join(pkgDir, 'README.md'))`; packages/v6y/package.json:12 `files: [dist, *.js, *.d.ts, README.md, LICENSE]`. The local copy is also stale (diff README.md packages/v6y/README.md shows the whole 'Fix automatically' section missing), harmless because it is gitignored (.gitignore:6) but a sign the copy step is easy to forget.
impact: The npm page, the second place adopters look, will have dead links to the example, the rule reference and the agents guide.
fix: In bundle.mjs rewrite `](./` links to `](https://github.com/walmat/v6y/blob/main/` (or use absolute links in README), and make `npm run build` part of `prepack`.

title: Sample outputs in both READMEs are stale (line numbers, wording, missing docs line)
claim: The example README's sample says the nested pressable is at `ProductCard.tsx:28:9`; it is at line 29. Both READMEs show `used at src/screens/menu/Before.tsx:17, 18` for the IconButton issue, but the current formatter prints `inside this shared component; fix it once. Used at …` and a `docs: https://…` line that neither sample shows.
evidence: `sed -n 24,32p examples/expo-app/src/components/before/ProductCard.tsx`: the `<Pressable … style={styles.heart}>` is line 29; `v6y check` on the example prints `at src/components/before/ProductCard.tsx:29:9`. packages/cli/src/format.ts:55 (component-scope wording) and :58 (`docs:` line). README.md:8-16 and examples/expo-app/README.md:10-22.
impact: The first thing a reader compares with a real run differs from it, which undermines the 'points at the line of code' promise.
fix: Paste the samples from a real run (`NO_COLOR=1 npm run a11y:check` in the example) and mark elisions with `…`; consider a test that checks README samples against formatter output for the example snapshot.

title: 'missing-heading … only in strict' is inaccurate
claim: Known gaps says missing-heading 'is only in `strict`', but it is a warning in `strict`, `wcag21-aa` and `wcag22-aa`; only `recommended` turns it off.
evidence: packages/core/src/config.ts:73 (strict: warning), :81-86 (wcag21aa spreads strict), :89-92 (wcag22aa spreads wcag21aa); docs/rules/README.md:17 and README.md:178 table both show warn/warn/warn.
impact: Users of the WCAG presets are surprised by heading warnings on every native-stack screen.
fix: Change to 'That's why it is off in `recommended` and a warning (never an error) elsewhere; disable it per screen with `screens.ignore` or set it to off if your headers come from native navigation bars.'

title: CI advice pins the Action to `@main`, inputs are undocumented and there are no tags
claim: The README workflow uses `walmat/v6y@main`, so every push to main changes users' CI gate, and the Action's `snapshots`, `working-directory` and `changed-only` inputs (needed for monorepos) appear nowhere in the docs.
evidence: README.md:201; action.yml:8-17 defines the three inputs; `git tag` → none; docs/agents.md and README never mention `working-directory`.
impact: Monorepo users cannot find how to point the action at their app; `@main` makes CI results drift without a visible change.
fix: Tag v0.1.0 and recommend `walmat/v6y@v0`; add a small inputs table under 'CI and pre-commit'.

title: Help text column misaligned; `--json`, `V6Y_DISABLE`, `withV6y` options and `pollMs` undocumented
claim: The `v6y dev [--port ${DEFAULT_PORT}]` line is padded before interpolation, so its description column is off by eight spaces in the real output; `--json` is accepted (bin.ts:67) but not in HELP; `V6Y_DISABLE=1` and `withV6y(config, { enabled, entry })` exist only in code comments; `capture.pollMs` exists only in the config type.
evidence: Reproduced `v6y help`: 'v6y dev [--port 8973]        Standalone report server' vs the aligned rows above it. packages/metro/src/index.ts:24-29 (`enabled`, `entry`), :84 (`V6Y_DISABLE`); packages/core/src/config.ts:38-39 (`pollMs`). `grep -c V6Y_DISABLE README.md` → 0.
impact: Users who need to turn v6y off for a build, point it at a non-standard entry, or tune polling have to read the source.
fix: Build HELP rows with `padEnd` after interpolation; document `--json` or drop it; add a 'Turning it off' note (`V6Y_DISABLE=1`, `withV6y(config, { enabled: false })`) and the `entry` option under Setup; add `pollMs` to the config sample.

title: Snapshot staleness is mtime-based, so a git checkout makes `fix` skip and `--changed` warn although nothing changed
claim: README:96 says `fix` 'won't edit a file that changed since its snapshot was taken'; the check is `fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs > capturedAt`, which also fires after `git checkout`, `stash`, branch switches or a fresh clone, producing 'file changed since the snapshot; re-run its test first' and stale-snapshot warnings for files whose content is identical.
evidence: fix.ts:213-221 and packages/cli/src/changed.ts:97-107 compare mtime with `capturedAt`. The example on disk shows the pattern: sources at 16:58:02 are newer than snapshots at 16:58:01 after what looks like a revert (ls --time-style=full-iso).
impact: In CI with a fresh checkout every file is 'newer' than any committed or cached snapshot, so recorded snapshots are only usable when produced in the same job; locally, switching branches silently disables `fix`.
fix: Record a content hash per referenced source file in the snapshot (collector or at save time) and compare hashes, falling back to mtime; say 'content changed' in the message.

title: Nothing confirms v6y is active at Metro start-up; a silent first run is indistinguishable from a broken one
claim: `withV6y` prints nothing on success (only a warning when the entry is not found), and the app swallows failed report POSTs, so a user whose entry file was not detected, whose device cannot reach the dev-server origin, or who simply has not navigated yet sees an empty Metro terminal with no way to tell which case they are in.
evidence: metro/src/index.ts:91-93 is the only log in `withV6y`; packages/react-native/src/index.tsx:161-171 `send()` catches and ignores errors ('No dev server listening; the console summary is enough'). README:35 only says 'issues appear in the Metro terminal'.
impact: Onboarding confidence: the README's promise of output in the terminal has no visible 'ready' state, and the most common misconfigurations fail silently.
fix: Log one line from `withV6y` ('[v6y] on · config v6y.config.ts (strict) · entry src/App.tsx · reports at /v6y/report') and have the app log the endpoint once on the first failed send (`[v6y] could not reach <endpoint>; set configure({}, { endpoint })`).

title: loadConfig never reloads a .ts/.js/.mjs config within one process (only .json)
claim: `loadConfig` imports the config with `dynamicImport(pathToFileURL(file).href)` and the ESM loader caches by URL, so every call after the first returns the original module even after the file is edited; only the `.json` branch (fs.readFileSync) sees edits.
evidence: Probe against packages/cli/dist/index.js: wrote v6y.config.{mjs,js,json} with failOn:'error', called loadConfig, rewrote with failOn:'never', called again -> mjs: STALE, js: STALE, json: RELOADED. Callers that rely on per-call loading: `analyze()` (line 124) used by every `check_accessibility`/`fix_accessibility` call in the long-lived `v6y mcp` server (mcp.ts:125,151), `dev()` (line 247) and the Metro middleware `receive()` (metro/src/index.ts:132). No test edits a config between two loads (cli.test.ts loads each config once).
impact: An agent or developer who edits v6y.config.ts during an MCP session (add an ignore, turn a rule off, change failOn) keeps getting results from the old config until the server is restarted, with no indication why; same for `v6y dev` / Metro re-audits of raw snapshots. `v6y check` is unaffected (one process per run).
fix: Cache-bust the import URL with the file's mtime (`pathToFileURL(file).href + '?v=' + fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs`) and `delete createRequire(file).cache[file]` before the require() fallback; add a cli.test.ts case that loads, edits and reloads a .mjs and a .ts config and asserts the new value.

title: The GitHub Action is never verified: the dogfood step is PR-only and continue-on-error
claim: The only execution of action.yml in CI runs under `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` with `continue-on-error: true`, so it never runs on push to main and cannot fail a PR whatever happens, and nothing else exercises the composite action's bash.
evidence: ci.yml lines 45-50: `- name: v6y on changed files`, `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, `uses: ./`, `continue-on-error: true`. The step is expected to exit 1 anyway (the example's Before screens have errors by design, comment on lines 43-44), so a genuine failure (`v6y isn't installed` exit 1 from action.yml line 32, a bash error, `npx --no-install` not resolving) is indistinguishable from the expected one and is swallowed. No unit test covers action.yml, integrations/claude-code/hooks/pre-commit-check.mjs or .mcp.json either.
impact: README tells users to pin `uses: walmat/v6y@main`; a regression in action.yml or in `v6y check --format github --base` lands on main unnoticed and breaks every adopter's PR check at once.
fix: Give the step an `id`, run it on push too with `changed-only: 'false'`, keep `continue-on-error: true`, then add a step that asserts `steps.v6y.outcome == 'failure'` (the Before screens must be caught) and a second run against only the `*.after.json` snapshots that must succeed; grep the job log or a `--format github` run for `^::error file=` to prove annotations were emitted. Add a small test that feeds pre-commit-check.mjs a fake PreToolUse event.

title: Test files do not type-check and no tsconfig or CI step ever tries
claim: Every package tsconfig includes only `src`, so tests are never compiled by tsc; under the shared base config they fail with 8x TS1343 (`import.meta` is not allowed with `module: CommonJS`) and 2x TS7016 (`react-test-renderer` has no declarations because `@types/react-test-renderer` is not a devDependency), and the TS7016 errors persist even under an ESM/Bundler config.
evidence: Ran `tsc -p` with a scratchpad tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.json over packages/*/test: TS1343 in cli/test/fix.test.ts:7, mcp.test.ts:80, core/test/docs.test.ts:6, metro/test/metro.test.ts:13-14, v6y/test/bundle.test.ts:7-8; TS7016 in react-native/test/collect.test.tsx:3 and jest-matcher.test.tsx:3. With module ESNext/moduleResolution Bundler only the two TS7016 remain. ci.yml runs only `npm test` (vitest). The `as any` casts in the tests hide no API drift (no other errors), but nothing would catch drift in future.
impact: A signature change in core/cli/react-native breaks tests only at runtime (or silently, where a test passes `any`), and the test suite cannot be used as a typed usage example of the public API.
fix: Add `@types/react-test-renderer` to root devDependencies; add a root `tsconfig.test.json` (noEmit, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, jsx react, `paths` mirroring the vitest aliases, include packages/*/test) and a `typecheck` script run in CI (or enable vitest's `typecheck` mode).

title: `v6y fix` leaves a lone CR when removing an attribute from a CRLF file
claim: The remove-attr splice trims the attribute's leading indentation and one `\n` but not a preceding `\r`, so on CRLF sources the removed line's `\r` survives and the file ends up with a bare CR followed by CRLF.
evidence: Probe against packages/cli/dist/fix.js on a CRLF file with multi-line opening elements: result contains `<Text<CR><CR>\n` (one `\r` left behind), `lone CR present: true`; add-attr on the multi-line `<Pressable` worked correctly. fix.ts lines 157-164 only test for `[ \t]` and `'\n'`. fix.test.ts has no CRLF or multi-line-attribute case.
impact: Windows / `core.autocrlf=true` repos get mixed line endings on the edited line after `v6y fix`: git warns 'CRLF will be replaced', Prettier/ESLint linebreak-style flags it, and the diff shows a changed line beyond the fix.
fix: After `if (text[start - 1] === '\n') { start--; ... }` also consume a `\r` (`if (text[start - 1] === '\r') start--;`) before trimming the previous line's indentation; add fix.test.ts cases for a CRLF file and for attributes on their own lines.

title: `v6y/jest` auto-registration is a silent no-op under Vitest unless globals:true
claim: Registration happens via `(globalThis as any).expect?.extend`, which is undefined under Vitest's default `globals: false`, so `setupFiles: ['v6y/jest']` registers nothing and `expect(x).toBeAccessible()` throws 'Invalid Chai property', while README.md:227 advertises the matcher 'for Jest and Vitest' with only Jest setup instructions.
evidence: Vitest probe with `setupFiles: ['/…/packages/v6y/jest.js']`: globals:false -> `Error: Invalid Chai property: toBeAccessible`; globals:true -> passes. The repo's own Vitest test sidesteps this by calling `expect.extend(matchers as any)` itself (jest-matcher.test.tsx:7), so the auto path is untested in Vitest. (Typing is fine: Vitest's JestAssertion extends jest.Matchers, verified with tsc, so the `as any` casts there are unnecessary.)
impact: A Vitest user following the README gets a runtime error with no hint that `globals: true` is required.
fix: Document `globals: true` for Vitest, or ship a `v6y/vitest` entry that does `import { expect } from 'vitest'; expect.extend(matchers)`; add a Vitest test that loads the matcher through `setupFiles` (not a manual extend) and drop the `as any` casts in jest-matcher.test.tsx.

title: The in-app runtime and the RNTL path of toBeAccessible have no tests at all
claim: `V6yProvider.startWatching` (poll/debounce with capture.pollMs/delayMs), `trackNavigation`, `devServerEndpoint` (scriptURL parsing incl. bridgeless getConstants), `send`, `logSummary`, `configure` fallback on invalid config, auto.ts (project-config require + AppRegistry wrapper), `defaultMeasure`'s three Paper/Fabric branches and 500 ms timeout (collect.ts:416-437), and `hostTypes.modal` are not referenced by any test; neither is `fiberOf`'s `UNSAFE_root`/`root._fiber` path (jest.ts:51-55) that the README's first example `expect(render(<Checkout />)).toBeAccessible()` relies on.
evidence: grep for defaultMeasure|trackNavigation|devServerEndpoint|startWatching|setWrapperComponentProvider|`hostTypes: { modal` across packages/*/test and examples/expo-app/src/__tests__ returns nothing; `@testing-library` appears only in the example's package-lock.json. collect.test.tsx covers collect() only through V6yProvider with autoCapture:false; jest-matcher tests pass elements or a raw react-test-renderer instance. README.md:247 admits the device runtime is unverified, but all of the above is pure JS testable with fake timers and stubbed `react-native`/stateNodes.
impact: The code path every real app runs (auto wrapper, poll, capture, POST to Metro) and the headline test API for RNTL users can regress without any test failing; the field tests only exercised capture() manually.
fix: Add react-native/test/runtime.test.tsx using vi.useFakeTimers and a stubbed `react-native` module: provider mounts, polls, captures once per route change after delayMs, posts to the scriptURL origin; trackNavigation; configure() with an invalid config falls back; defaultMeasure with fake Paper/Fabric stateNodes incl. timeout. Add @testing-library/react-native as a devDependency and one RNTL render() assertion; add a hostTypes.modal case to collect.test.tsx.

title: The `v6y` binary's argument parsing and exit codes are untested
claim: Only the `mcp` subcommand is ever executed through dist/bin.js (mcp.test.ts:79-111); `check`/`fix`/`init`/`rules`/`dev` flag parsing, `--format` validation, `--json`, `--port`, the positional filter, unknown-command exit 2 and the `process.exitCode` contract that CI and the Action depend on are only exercised via the library functions.
evidence: cli.test.ts calls check()/init()/dev() directly; no test spawns `bin.js check`. By reading bin.ts:25-31 and 67, `option()` matches an exact `--format` token and the positional filter drops anything starting with `--`, so `v6y check snaps --format=github` or a typo like `--changedd` is silently ignored and prints text with exit 0/1 as for a plain check; a test would catch that.
impact: The one surface users and action.yml actually invoke can drift from the tested library functions; silent acceptance of mistyped flags makes CI appear to pass with the wrong mode.
fix: Add cli/test/bin.test.ts that spawns dist/bin.js for `check` (exit 1 on errors, 0 with failOn never, 2 with no files / bad --format), `--format github` output, `fix --dry-run`, `init`, `rules`, unknown command; reject unknown `--flags` and support `--flag=value` in bin.ts.

title: fix / MCP fix_accessibility / changed.ts have untested branches
claim: The `fix_accessibility` MCP tool (mcp.ts:146-160), `ping` and the -32700 parse-error reply (mcp.ts:189, 217), `fix` with `--changed`, the `set-attr` maxFontSizeMultiplier and `missing-heading` edits (fix.ts:74-85), the 'element not found' and 'file not found' skips, and in changed.ts the rename/delete/outside-git/shallow-merge-base paths and `--base` through check()/coverage() are not covered.
evidence: mcp.test.ts only asserts the tool name in tools/list (line 74) and calls check_accessibility/explain_rule/list_rules; fix.test.ts covers add-attr, remove-attr, idempotence, dry-run and stale-file only; changed.test.ts asserts `--base` via changedFiles() only (line 83-91) and never hits the catch at changed.ts:35-38 or 50-54.
impact: The agent-facing fix tool and the diff logic the Action relies on can break silently, e.g. a wrong `changed` object shape passed from mcp.ts to fix() would not be caught.
fix: Add callTool('fix_accessibility') tests (dry-run and applied, structuredContent shape); add fix cases for maxFontSizeMultiplier, heading, --changed, element-not-found; add changed.ts cases for a staged rename, a deleted file, a non-git cwd, and check() with `--base` asserting the coverage warnings.

title: CI runs one Node version and packages declare no engines, so the documented Node floor is never exercised
claim: Both jobs run on Node 24 only, while README.md:131 promises TypeScript configs on Node >= 22.18 and loadConfig has a Node-version-specific fallback (`ERR_VM_DYNAMIC_IMPORT_CALLBACK_MISSING` -> require(esm), index.ts:49-52) and error message (index.ts:58-60); vitest.config.mts:8 uses `import.meta.dirname` (Node >= 20.11) and no package.json has an `engines` field.
evidence: ci.yml lines 16 and 30 `node-version: 24`; grep '"engines"' package.json packages/*/package.json -> none; cli.test.ts:55-62 loads a .ts config only on the local Node 24.
impact: A user on Node 22.x or 20 gets behaviour nobody tested (the friendly 'needs Node 22.18' message, or an opaque failure), and `npm i -D v6y` gives no warning on unsupported Node.
fix: Add `engines: { node: '>=22.12' }` (or whatever floor you support) to packages/v6y/package.json and a `node-version: [22, 24]` matrix for the Packages job; add a test for loadConfig's TS-on-old-Node error path by stubbing the import to throw ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION.

title: MCP stdio test's own 10 s guard can never fire and the child is leaked on timeout
claim: Vitest's default testTimeout is 5000 ms, so the test's 10 s `setTimeout(reject)` and its diagnostic `timeout; got …` are unreachable; on a slow runner the test fails with the generic vitest timeout and `child.kill()` (line 107) never runs.
evidence: node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/resolveConfig.*.js:8313 `testTimeout ??= … 5e3`; vitest.config.mts sets no testTimeout; the `it` at line 79 passes no timeout; the 20 ms setInterval poll (line 99) keeps spinning until vitest aborts.
impact: Flaky failure mode under CI load with a useless message and an orphaned `node dist/bin.js mcp` process until stdin closes.
fix: Pass `{ timeout: 15_000 }` to the `it`, resolve from the stdout 'data' handler instead of polling, and kill the child in a `finally`.

title: Temp directories are created by five test files and never removed
claim: cli.test.ts:30, changed.test.ts:17, mcp.test.ts:15 and 49, metro.test.ts:20 and jest-matcher.test.tsx:66 all `mkdtempSync` under os.tmpdir() with no afterAll/onTestFinished cleanup; only fix.test.ts:9 cleans up.
evidence: `ls -d /tmp/v6y-*` on this machine: 538 leftover directories (341 v6y-, 102 v6y-git-, 39 v6y-metro-, 31 v6y-mcp-, 17 v6y-snaps-, 8 v6y-mcp-empty-), the git ones each a full repository.
impact: Hundreds of stray repos per developer over time; on shared CI runners they accumulate within a job's lifetime only, but locally they never go away.
fix: Add a shared test helper `tmpDir()` that registers `onTestFinished(() => fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))`, and use it everywhere.

title: The dev-server test runs `adb reverse tcp:0 tcp:0` on the developer's machine
claim: `dev()` unconditionally calls `adbReverse(port)` in the listen callback with the requested port, so cli.test.ts:83 (`dev({ port: 0 })`) executes `adb reverse tcp:0 tcp:0` whenever adb is installed, and with an attached device actually creates a bogus reverse.
evidence: index.ts:257-268: `server.listen(port, () => { …; adbReverse(port); })` and `execFile('adb', ['reverse', 'tcp:'+port, 'tcp:'+port])`; the test passes port 0 and only mocks console.log.
impact: Tests have a side effect outside the sandbox; harmless on CI, surprising on a dev machine with a device plugged in.
fix: Skip adb when the requested port is 0, or add a `{ adb?: boolean }` option to dev() that the test sets to false; use the bound port from server.address() for the real call.

title: No lint or format step, yet 15 eslint-disable directives assume ESLint
claim: There is no ESLint/Prettier/Biome config or `lint` script anywhere and CI runs none, but packages/*/src carries 15 `eslint-disable` comments written for a setup that does not exist.
evidence: `grep -rn eslint-disable packages/*/src | wc -l` = 15; `ls -a | grep -iE 'eslint|prettierrc|biome'` empty; no `"lint"` in any package.json; ci.yml has only `npm ci` and `npm test`.
impact: Unused `any`s, unused imports and style drift go unnoticed; the directives are dead weight that misleads contributors about the toolchain.
fix: Add eslint + typescript-eslint (and prettier or biome) with a `lint` script and a CI step, or delete the directives.

title: Misnamed config test, duplicated example mocks, unnecessary casts
claim: The test titled 'loads v6y.config.js and v6y.config.ts' writes v6y.config.mjs, so CommonJS `v6y.config.js` (the common React Native shape) is only exercised indirectly by metro.test.ts:23; examples/expo-app/src/__tests__/matcher.test.tsx:11-22 and showcase.test.tsx:33-48 duplicate the expo-router and @expo/vector-icons mocks with different Ionicons implementations (empty string vs the PUA glyph with allowFontScaling:false); jest-matcher.test.tsx casts `expect(...) as any` although Vitest already types jest.Matchers augmentations.
evidence: cli.test.ts:57 `v6y.config.mjs`; both example test files define `jest.mock('@expo/vector-icons', …)` with different bodies; a scratchpad tsc run of `await expect(1).toBeAccessible()` under Vitest types passed while a bogus matcher failed with TS2339.
impact: Readers are told something is tested that is not; the two Ionicons mocks can drift and make one example test lie about icon handling; the casts hide the typed API.
fix: Rename the test and add a `module.exports` v6y.config.js case; move the mocks to examples/expo-app/__mocks__/@expo/vector-icons.js and __mocks__/expo-router.js; remove the `as any` casts.

title: Example app lists jest, jest-expo and @types/jest as runtime dependencies
claim: `@types/jest` (line 8), `jest` (line 22) and `jest-expo` (line 23) are in `dependencies` while react-test-renderer, typescript and v6y are correctly in devDependencies.
evidence: Read of examples/expo-app/package.json; node probe printing each key's section.
impact: Cosmetic for an example, but it is the project people copy the jest setup from.
fix: Move the three to devDependencies.

title: vitest.config.mts says tests run against sources, but three files require a built dist/
claim: metro.test.ts (createRequire of packages/metro/dist), bundle.test.ts (packages/v6y/dist) and the mcp stdio test (packages/cli/dist/bin.js) need `npm run build` first; `npx vitest run` on a fresh clone fails them with MODULE_NOT_FOUND and nothing says why.
evidence: vitest.config.mts:6 comment; metro.test.ts:14,36; bundle.test.ts:7,18; mcp.test.ts:80; only the `npm test` script chains the build.
impact: Contributors running vitest directly (or an editor's test runner) see confusing failures.
fix: Correct the comment and add a tiny `globalSetup` that checks the three dist entry points exist and fails with 'run npm run build'.

title: Several rule options and report-formatter branches have no unit test
claim: `meaningless-label` options `allow` (only via the example's v6y.config.ts) and `generic`, `duplicate-label` `ignoreCase`, `touch-target-size` `ios`/`android`, and `font-scaling-disabled` `minMultiplier` are never set in any unit test; formatIssues' component-scope line ('inside this shared component'), the `+N more` call-site truncation and the '(no source…)' hint are never asserted.
evidence: grep of packages/*/test and the example tests for each option name; grep for 'inside this shared component|MAX_SITES|no source:' in packages/cli/test returns nothing.
impact: Documented options can silently stop working; the README's sample report lines are produced by untested formatter branches.
fix: Add option cases to config.test.ts (each option on and off) and formatIssues cases for scope:'component', >4 call sites and an issue without source.

title: accessible={false} pressables are audited as if they were accessibility elements
claim: missing-role, missing-label and duplicate-label never look at node.accessible, so a pressable with accessible={false} (the exact pattern nested-interactive tells users to adopt) is reported as 'has no role'/'has no accessible name', and `v6y fix` writes accessibilityRole="button" onto an element that is not an accessibility element.
evidence: roles.ts:17 `if (!node.interactive || node.role || hasIntrinsicRole(node)) return [];` and names.ts:19/176 have no accessible check; only nestedInteractive (roles.ts:41) honours `accessible !== false`. Probe: {interactive, accessible:false, children:[Text role=button 'Go']} -> missing-role with fix 'Add accessibilityRole="button"'; {interactive, accessible:false, children:[Image]} -> missing-label + missing-role; outer accessible=false wrapper around an inner 'Like' button (strict) -> missing-role on the wrapper plus duplicate-label on BOTH the wrapper and the inner button (wrapper's merged name equals the child's). RN Pressable.js:276 sets `accessible: accessible !== false` on the host, i.e. iOS isAccessibilityElement=NO; fix.ts:70-71 adds the role at issue.source with no node check. REPORT.md item 11 asked for this ('report as unreachable, not no role') and it was not implemented.
impact: False positives on a recommended pattern (users who follow nested-interactive's own fix get a new missing-role error), a no-op autofix, and the real defect (a control with no accessible descendants is unreachable) is mis-described.
fix: In missing-role/missing-label/duplicate-label skip nodes with `accessible === false`. Add an 'unreachable-control' finding (or extend missing-label) for an interactive node with `accessible === false` whose non-hidden descendants contain no Text, no `accessible` node and no interactive node, with the fix 'remove accessible={false} or make a child the accessible control'. In fix.ts, never add a role to an element whose node has accessible===false. Add tests for all three rules.

title: touch-target-size reports hard 2.5.8 failures without any of 2.5.8's exceptions; inline text links get an error and an impossible hitSlop fix
claim: Any interactive node under 24pt in either dimension is reported at the rule's level (error in recommended/strict/wcag22-aa) citing 2.5.8, but 2.5.8 exempts inline targets (links in a line of text), spaced undersized targets, equivalent targets, essential and user-agent-controlled ones; a `<Text onPress>` link is therefore a false WCAG failure, and `v6y fix` then adds a `hitSlop` prop that Text does not have.
evidence: visual.ts:43-49 only tests `w < o.minimum || h < o.minimum`. Probe: RCTText {interactive, role:'link', frame 120x17} -> 'touch target is 120×17, below the minimum of 24×24' (error). fix.ts:77-80 plans `hitSlop={16}` for every touch-target issue regardless of node type; `grep -rn hitSlop Libraries/Text/` in RN 0.88 returns nothing (Text has no hitSlop prop). Frames carry x/y (types.ts:22-27) so the spacing exception is computable but unused.
impact: Every text link on a device capture becomes a blocking CI error that the cited criterion does not require; the autofix emits an unsupported prop.
fix: Treat text-kind interactive nodes (isText) as inline: skip the 24×24 minimum (keep the advisory). Implement the spacing exception using the collected frames: an undersized target passes when a 24pt circle centred on its box intersects no other target. Skip disabled targets. In fix.ts only plan hitSlop for non-text nodes. Document the exceptions in the rule docs.

title: Advisory 44/48pt touch-target warnings cite 2.5.8, which they pass; the defined 2.5.5 criterion is never used
claim: The platform-guideline advisory finding inherits the rule's wcag ['2.5.8'] although a 40×40 target satisfies 2.5.8 (24×24); WCAG['2.5.5'] Target Size (Enhanced, AAA, 44×44) exists in wcag.ts but no rule references it, unlike text-contrast which correctly overrides to 1.4.6 for AAA.
evidence: visual.ts:51-58 returns `{advisory:true, message, fix}` with no `wcag` override; engine.ts:28 uses `f.wcag ?? wcag`. Probe: 40×40 button on ios -> severity 'warning', wcag ['2.5.8'], message 'below the Apple HIG recommendation of 44×44'. `grep -rn 2.5.5 packages/` hits only wcag.ts:20. Compare visual.ts:128 `wcag: o.level === 'AAA' ? ['1.4.6'] : undefined`.
impact: Reports, PR annotations and compliance exports label a passing target as a WCAG 2.5.8 issue; the wcag22-aa preset only avoids this because it disables platformGuidelines.
fix: Set `wcag: ['2.5.5']` on the advisory finding (and say 'Apple HIG / Material; WCAG AAA 2.5.5' in the message), add a test asserting the advisory's wcag, and note in the docs that 2.5.8 is the error and 2.5.5/platform guidelines are the warning.

title: parseColor misses hsl/hsla/hwb and most CSS named colours that React Native accepts, so contrast is silently skipped
claim: parseColor returns undefined for hsl(), hsla(), hwb() and ~120 of the 150 named colours React Native's normalize-colors accepts, and text-contrast treats undefined as 'unknown colour' and skips the text with no warning, producing false negatives.
evidence: color.ts:11-42 lists ~30 names; lines 57-78 handle only #hex and rgb/rgba. Probe: parseColor('hsl(0, 100%, 50%)'), 'hsla(0,100%,50%,0.5)', 'hwb(0 0% 0%)', 'tomato', 'slategray', 'rebeccapurple' -> undefined; RN 0.88 @react-native/normalize-colors returns ff0000ff / ff6347ff for the same inputs and has 150 `case '<name>'` entries (index.js:126-180 hsl/hsla/hwb matchers). Probe: Text color 'hsl(0, 0%, 70%)' on #fff -> no text-contrast issue although #b3b3b3 on white is 2.0:1.
impact: Apps using hsl tokens (common in design systems) or named colours get a clean contrast report for failing text.
fix: Port the hsl/hsla/hwb conversion and the full named-colour table from @react-native/normalize-colors (or depend on it; it is pure JS and already in every RN project), and have text-contrast emit a one-off debug note when a colour string is unparseable rather than failing silently. Add parseColor tests for these forms.

title: Collector stringifies numeric (processed) colours, making parseColor's 0xAARRGGBB branch dead and losing the colour
claim: pickStyle converts a numeric style colour to a decimal string ('4278190335'), which parseColor's string path cannot parse, so processed colours are dropped even though parseColor explicitly supports numbers and is tested with one.
evidence: collect.ts:93-95 `if (typeof flat.color === 'string' || typeof flat.color === 'number') s.color = String(flat.color)`; color.ts:46-50 handles `typeof input === 'number'`; rules.test.ts:30 tests parseColor(0xff0000ff). Probe: parseColor(String(0xff0000ff)) -> undefined; a Text with color String(0xffbbbbbb) on #fff -> no text-contrast issue.
impact: Any style that reaches the host as a processed int (processColor(), some animated/native-driven styles) is silently skipped by text-contrast; the unit test gives false assurance.
