fix: Keep numbers as numbers: widen NodeStyle.color/backgroundColor to `string | number` (types.ts:45-46) and store `flat.color` unchanged, or convert ints to '#rrggbbaa' in pickStyle. Add a collector test with a numeric colour.

title: style.opacity is collected but ignored, so dimmed text passes contrast
claim: NodeStyle.opacity is captured by the collector but neither effectiveTextColor nor effectiveBackground applies it, so text under `opacity: 0.3` (or with its own opacity) is checked at full strength and passes.
evidence: types.ts:49 declares opacity; collect.ts:98 records it; `grep -rn opacity packages/core/src` finds no use outside types.ts. Probe: {bg #fff} > View {opacity:0.3} > Text {color:#000} 'Faint' -> no issues, although black at 30% over white is ~#b3b3b3 (≈2.0:1).
impact: A very common way of rendering secondary/disabled-looking text (`opacity: 0.5`) is never flagged, a false negative at error level.
fix: In text-contrast, multiply the text colour's alpha by the product of `style.opacity` of the node and every ancestor up to the opaque background layer before blending (opacity applies to the whole subtree, so apply the same factor to translucent background layers above the opaque base). Add a test. If opacity is intentionally unsupported, drop the field from NodeStyle.

title: README says text over images/gradients is skipped; text-contrast actually uses the nearest ancestor backgroundColor (field-test FP #35 still open)
claim: The known-gaps note claims 'Text with unknown colors (theme defaults, images, gradients) is skipped', but effectiveBackground has no notion of ImageBackground, absolutely positioned images or gradient hosts and composites whatever backgroundColor it finds up the chain, so text on an image inside a coloured container is checked against the container colour.
evidence: tree.ts:65-79 walks `style.backgroundColor` only; nothing in core references image or gradient kinds. REPORT.md #35 (splash 'Sign in' over an image, FP) and REPORT-v2.md §3 'Remaining: #35 … The image-background fix was not in this change'. visual.ts:98 docs repeat the same claim.
impact: Users read the README, trust the skip, and get error-level contrast failures with a suggested colour that is wrong for the real backdrop.
fix: Either implement the skip (mark nodes whose kind is image/gradient, or any absolutely positioned sibling earlier in the parent with an image kind, as an unknown layer and return undefined from effectiveBackground when one sits between the text and the opaque colour) or change README.md:250 and visual.ts:98 to say that image and gradient backgrounds are not detected and may need v6y-ignore.

title: meaningless-label flags hyphenated words and i/e-prefixed product names as code identifiers
claim: IDENTIFIER (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)+$`) matches any hyphenated word and CAMEL (`^[a-z]+[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`) matches lower-camel product names, so ordinary labels are reported as 'looks like a code identifier'.
evidence: Probe meaninglessLabelReason(label,'button'): 'Wi-Fi', 'E-mail', 'Check-in', 'Sign-up', 'Opt-out', 'Re-order', 'Add-on', 'T-shirt', 'Follow-up', 'iPhone', 'iCloud', 'macOS' all -> 'it looks like a code identifier'. 'More' -> 'generic' (Apple's own overflow label).
impact: Warning-level noise on correct labels in every preset; erodes trust in a heuristic rule.
fix: Require an underscore, a digit, or 3+ segments for IDENTIFIER (`ic_close`, `icon_23`, `btn-add-to-cart`) and exempt single-hyphen two-word labels; for CAMEL require the lowercase prefix to be 2+ chars and not in {i, e, mac, tv, watch} or keep a small allowlist of product names; consider removing 'more' from GENERIC. Add the above strings as accept-cases in rules.test.ts.

title: input-missing-label accepts accessibilityLabelledBy alone and recommends it, but iOS does not implement it
claim: A TextInput with only labelledBy passes, and the fix/docs text present accessibilityLabelledBy/aria-labelledby as a sufficient alternative to accessibilityLabel, yet React Native implements accessibilityLabelledBy only on Android, so on iOS such a field is announced with no name.
evidence: names.ts:136 `if (node.label?.trim() || node.labelledBy) return [];`, fix at :144 'or link a visible label with accessibilityLabelledBy', docs at :131. RN 0.88 sources: `accessibilityLabelledBy` appears only under ReactAndroid (ViewProps.kt:170, ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:60/91); grep of React/ (iOS) finds no handler. Probe: input {labelledBy:'lbl'} on platform ios -> no issues.
impact: False negative on iOS plus a fix that users apply and that does nothing for VoiceOver; the 'good' example in examples.ts:25-26 happens to also set accessibilityLabel, so the docs and the check disagree.
fix: Accept labelledBy only when snapshot.platform === 'android'; on ios (and unknown) report 'labelled only via accessibilityLabelledBy, which iOS ignores' with the fix 'add accessibilityLabel as well'. Update the docs/fix text accordingly.

title: Image `alt` is never read, so in Jest an Image with alt plus role/accessible is reported as unlabelled
claim: The collector derives label only from accessibilityLabel/aria-label; on a device Image.ios.js rewrites alt into accessibilityLabel before the host, but React Native's Jest Image mock passes props through untouched, so under `toBeAccessible()` an `<Image alt="…" role="img">` (or `accessible alt`) triggers image-missing-label.
evidence: collect.ts:302-303 `p.accessibilityLabel ?? p['aria-label']`. RN 0.88 Libraries/Image/Image.ios.js:198-215 maps alt -> accessibilityLabel and accessible=true; @react-native/jest-preset/jest/setup.js:138 mocks Image with mockComponent, whose render (mockComponent.js:59-78) copies every defined prop to createElement('Image', props) with no alt handling. Probe: node {type:'Image', kind:'image', role:'img'} with no label -> image-missing-label.
impact: The documented primary CI path (Jest/RNTL) fails on the modern, correct way to label images; README's image example uses accessibilityLabel so users following the RN docs' alt prop hit it.
fix: In collect.ts read `p.alt` as a label fallback (and set accessible=true when alt is a string) for image-kind hosts; mention `alt` in image-missing-label's fix text and examples. Add a collector test rendering 'Image' with alt.

title: Unlabelled native Switch/Slider controls are never reported
claim: hasIntrinsicRole excludes Switch and Slider hosts from missing-label (and they are not `interactive` anyway, since their hosts carry onChange rather than onPress), and no other rule checks that a native toggle has a name, so a bare <Switch> beside a <Text> is silently accepted although VoiceOver/TalkBack announce only 'switch, off'.
evidence: tree.ts:25-27 `return isTextInput(node) || SWITCH_TYPES.test(node.type) || SLIDER_TYPES.test(node.type)`; names.ts:19 returns early on it; input-missing-label only handles isTextInput (names.ts:135). Probe: [Text 'Dark mode', RCTSwitch 51x31] -> no issues.
impact: One of the most frequent real-world mobile a11y bugs (toggle rows where the label is a sibling Text) is a guaranteed false negative in every preset.
fix: Add a `control-missing-label` rule (or extend input-missing-label to Switch/Slider/Checkbox kinds): flag a switch/slider host with no label/labelledBy/accessibleName and no non-hidden ancestor that is `accessible` with a name; fix text: 'add accessibilityLabel, or wrap the row in a View accessible accessibilityRole="switch" accessibilityState={{checked}}'. Make the collector mark these hosts (e.g. kind 'switch'/'slider') instead of regexing type in core.

title: Interactive content hidden from assistive technology is never reported
claim: The engine skips hidden subtrees entirely, so a pressable inside accessibilityElementsHidden / importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" / aria-hidden is unreachable to screen readers yet produces no issue; standard tools (axe aria-hidden-focus) treat this as an error.
evidence: engine.ts:39 `if (node.hidden) return;` with collect.ts:121-129 setting hidden for those props. Probe: {hidden:true, children:[button 'Buy' 48x48]} -> no issues. The only hidden-related handling is name merging (tree.ts:48).
impact: A whole class of 'control exists but cannot be operated with VoiceOver/TalkBack' defects is invisible to v6y.
fix: Add a `hidden-interactive` rule: in checkScreen walk snapshot.root including hidden subtrees and report interactive (or text-input/switch) nodes whose hidden flag comes from an explicit a11y-hiding prop (not display:none, inactive screens or modal pruning; have the collector record `hiddenBy`). Fix text: 'remove accessibilityElementsHidden / aria-hidden from the container, or disable the control while hidden'.

title: missing-heading's title heuristic can pick a button label and the autofix would mark it as a header
claim: findTitle accepts the first ≥20pt (or ≥16pt semibold) text anywhere, including text inside an interactive element, so a screen whose largest text is a big primary button gets '"Get started" looks like this screen's title' and `v6y fix` adds accessibilityRole="header" to the button's Text.
evidence: roles.ts:116-133 never checks interactive ancestors; fix.ts:72-76 plans the header role whenever the message starts with a quote. Probe (strict): one Pressable containing Text 'Get started' {fontSize:20, fontWeight:'700'} -> missing-heading pointing at it with fix 'Add accessibilityRole="header" to it.'
impact: Wrong element blamed and an autofix that gives a button a header trait.
fix: In findTitle skip texts with an interactive ancestor (track it in visit) and texts whose ancestor has a role; fall back to the generic 'no heading' message. Add a test.

title: touch-target-size hitSlop suggestion ignores the hitSlop the element already has
claim: The suggested value `ceil((guide - min(w,h))/2)` is computed from w/h that already include the existing hitSlop, so it suggests a smaller total slop than the element has.
evidence: visual.ts:37-39 add s.left/right into w; :56 uses w/h. Probe: 30×30 with hitSlop 4 (w=38) on ios -> 'Add hitSlop (e.g. hitSlop={3})', which would shrink the target to 36×36 if applied.
impact: Misleading fix text (fix.ts:78 skips nodes with hitSlop, so only the message is wrong).
fix: Compute from the raw frame: `Math.ceil((guide - Math.min(node.frame.width, node.frame.height)) / 2)`, and when hitSlop is already set say 'raise hitSlop to N'.

title: Math.round lets 23.5–23.99pt targets pass the 24pt minimum
claim: Width/height are rounded before comparison, so a 23.6×23.6 target is reported as 24×24 and passes 2.5.8, which requires at least 24.
evidence: visual.ts:38-39 `Math.round(...)`; probe 23.6×23.6 with platformGuidelines:false -> no touch-target issue.
impact: Marginal false negatives at the exact threshold.
fix: Compare unrounded values (or Math.floor) and round only for display.

title: font-scaling-disabled never checks TextInput although it has the same props
claim: The rule exits unless isText(node), and the collector only records allowFontScaling/maxFontSizeMultiplier for text-kind hosts, so `<TextInput allowFontScaling={false}>` or a capped multiplier on an input is never reported.
evidence: visual.ts:164 `if (!isText(node) || !hasSpeakableText(node)) return [];`; collect.ts:324-329 reads the props only when kind === 'text'. RN 0.88 TextInput.js:912/931 has allowFontScaling (default true) forwarded to the host. Probe: input {label:'Email', allowFontScaling:false} -> no issues.
impact: False negative for 1.4.4 on form fields, which are the text users most need to read.
fix: Record the two props for input kinds too and let the rule accept isText || isTextInput (no speakable-text requirement for inputs).

title: Fully transparent text is reported as a 1.00:1 contrast failure
claim: Text with color 'transparent' (alpha 0) is blended into the background and reported as failing with a suggested colour, although invisible text is not 'text' the user is meant to read (typically a sizing/measuring trick or an animated-in state).
evidence: visual.ts:109 `fgRaw.a < 1 ? blend(fgRaw, bg)`; effectiveBackground skips alpha-0 backgrounds (tree.ts:70) but no equivalent exists for the foreground. Probe: Text {color:'transparent'} on #fff -> 'has contrast 1.00:1 (#ffffff on #ffffff)… Use text color #757575'.
impact: Error-level FP in a rare but real pattern.
fix: Return [] when fgRaw.a === 0 (and optionally when the computed opacity is 0), mirroring the background handling.

title: missing-heading's 'no heading at all' finding cites criteria that do not require a heading
claim: The fallback finding 'This screen has no heading' carries wcag ['1.3.1','2.4.6'], but 1.3.1 only requires visually-styled headings to be programmatic (the 'looks like a title' variant) and 2.4.6 only governs headings that exist; WCAG has no AA requirement that a screen contain a heading (2.4.10 is AAA and 'where appropriate'), yet the wcag21-aa preset, described as 'requirements only', includes it.
evidence: roles.ts:139 meta.wcag, :158-166 fallback finding with no wcag override; config.ts:76-86 wcag21aa inherits strict's 'missing-heading': 'warning'; README.md:139 'Requirements only, no platform guidelines'.
impact: Compliance-oriented users get a non-requirement attributed to WCAG in a WCAG preset.
fix: Give the fallback finding `wcag: []` (or '2.4.10' with level AAA added to wcag.ts) and mark it advisory; keep 1.3.1 for the 'styled like a title' variant.

title: Rule tests do not cover the semantics the rules get wrong
claim: rules.test.ts and config.test.ts have no cases for accessible={false} pressables, opacity, hsl/named colours, numeric colours as the collector emits them, the advisory finding's wcag, inline text-link targets, Image alt, hidden interactive content, Switch labels or TextInput font scaling, so every finding above passes the suite.
evidence: Read both test files; the only colour-format test is rules.test.ts:25-32 and the only accessible-related test is config.test.ts:50-56 (nested-interactive).
impact: Regressions in these areas would go unnoticed; the suite does not pin the iOS/Android semantics the rules encode.
fix: Add a table-driven 'platform semantics' test block with the probes from this audit (the 17 constructed snapshots) as expectations once the fixes land.

title: Jest snapshot recording silently overwrites renders that share a test name
claim: record() names the file after snapshot.screen, which defaults to this.currentTestName, so two toBeAccessible() calls in one test (or two tests with the same title in different files) write the same <name>.<platform>.json and the earlier screen is lost.
evidence: jest.ts:116-117 builds the filename from snapshot.screen; toBeAccessible (jest.ts:122) sets screen = options.screen ?? this?.currentTestName. The example's own matcher.test.tsx asserts ProductBefore then AccountBefore inside 'the original screens are not'; examples/expo-app/.v6y/snapshots/the_original_screens_are_not.ios.json contains only the Account tree (14 nodes, texts 'Account', 'sam@example.com', 'Order history'...). The Product render is gone.
impact: v6y check, the GitHub Action, the MCP tools and the pre-commit gate never see the overwritten screen, so the CI gate has a silent hole exactly where users bundle assertions. Nothing warns.
fix: Default `screen` to the rendered root element's component name (element.type.displayName ?? name, or the RNTL container's first child) and keep the test title as metadata; suffix repeats within one test (#2, #3); in record(), refuse to overwrite a file written earlier in the same process (track written paths) and warn, or include a short content hash in the filename.

title: v6y fix joins issues to snapshots by `screen` only, so iOS+Android snapshots of one screen resolve node ids in the wrong tree
claim: byScreen is a Map keyed by snapshot.screen (last file wins) and issue.nodeId is a per-snapshot counter, so with two platform snapshots of the same screen the frames/props used to plan hitSlop and font-scaling edits come from a different element.
evidence: fix.ts:199 `new Map(snapshots.map((s) => [s.screen, ...]))`, :204-205 `byScreen.get(issue.screen)?.nodes.get(issue.nodeId)`, :213 staleness also uses that snapshot's capturedAt. Reproduced in a scratch project with Screen.ios.json (node 1 = 20x20 pressable) and Screen.android.json (node 1 = 200x40 text, node 2 = 40x40 pressable), both screen 'Screen': `fix` with the iOS file alone plans `hitSlop={14}`; with both files it plans `hitSlop={4}` (the iOS issue's node 1 was looked up in the Android tree). jest-expo multi-project setups (ios + android presets) produce exactly this pair of files.
impact: Wrong edits written into source (a 20x20 target gets hitSlop 4 -> 28x28, still failing); the next run then reports 'hitSlop is already set' and the issue has no path forward. The same shape of lookup makes stale-check and manual/auto classification wrong.
fix: Keep the snapshot with each issue in analyze() (e.g. return `{ issue, snapshot }` pairs or give Issue a `snapshotId` set by auditScreen) and look nodes up in that snapshot; never key by `screen` alone. Add a test with two platforms of one screen.

title: The documented non-Metro path (`import 'v6y/auto'` + `npx v6y dev`) cannot deliver reports: the runtime posts to the Metro origin and `v6y/auto` never sets `endpoint`
claim: devServerEndpoint() returns runtime.endpoint or `<bundle origin>/v6y/report`; `endpoint` is a RuntimeOption that cannot come from v6y.config.ts, and auto.ts calls configure() with only the project config, so an app set up per README line 45 posts to Metro (which has no /v6y/report handler without withV6y) and `v6y dev` on :8973 never receives anything.
evidence: index.tsx:65-72 (endpoint fallback; probe without RN prints http://localhost:8081/v6y/report), index.tsx:14-26 (RuntimeOptions 'not part of v6y.config.ts'), auto.ts:15-16 `configure(mod?.default ?? mod ?? {})`, cli/index.ts:235-262 `dev()` whose banner tells the user to call configure({}, { endpoint }) in app code, README:45 which mentions no such call. send() swallows the Metro 404 (index.tsx:161-171).
impact: A documented setup silently produces no output; users conclude v6y doesn't work. `v6y dev` (and its `/snapshot` alias route, cli/index.ts:241, unused since the initial commit) is a leftover from before the Metro middleware.
fix: Cut `v6y dev` and the `/snapshot` route: Metro is always running for an RN app, and withV6y composes with any existing config. If a no-withV6y path must stay, let the runtime read `endpoint` from a `dev`/`runtime` section of v6y.config.ts (or a V6Y_ENDPOINT baked in by the Babel plugin) and update README:45 accordingly.

title: `screens.ignore` is applied to the Jest default screen name (the test title), so a matching test passes with any tree
claim: auditRendered passes the test title as snapshot.screen into auditScreen, which returns { issues: [], skipped: true } when a screens.ignore glob matches; toBeAccessible never looks at `skipped`, so the assertion passes and `.not.toBeAccessible()` fails with 'found none'.
evidence: jest.ts:122 screen = options.screen ?? this?.currentTestName; jest.ts:102 and engine.ts:17 (screenIgnore test, skipped flag); jest.ts:126-138 only use result.issues. Probe against dist: auditScreen({ screen: 'Storybook renders the button', ... }, { screens: { ignore: ['Storybook*'] } }) -> {"issues":[],"suppressed":[],"skipped":true}; the same tree under another name reports missing-label and missing-role. README:123 recommends exactly 'Storybook*'.
impact: A silently green assertion; the two modes disagree on what `screen` means (device = route name, Jest = sentence), so screens.ignore, coverage/uncovered and fix cannot correlate a screen across modes.
fix: In the matcher, resolve the config with screenIgnore disabled (or throw 'screen X is ignored by screens.ignore' so the test is explicit), and default `screen` to the component name so the same screen has the same name in tests and on device.

title: Staleness and fix-safety rest on file mtime versus a capturedAt taken from the capturing process's clock
claim: coverage() and fix() decide 'snapshot older than your edits' by comparing fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs with Date.parse(capturedAt), where capturedAt is new Date() on the device (index.tsx:147) or in the Jest worker; neither the content nor the host clock is involved.
evidence: changed.ts:97-107, fix.ts:213-221, index.tsx:147, jest.ts:124. mtime changes on git checkout/stash/rebase, prettier --write and cache restores without any content change; a device clock that lags the host makes fresh captures look stale, one that leads makes edits after the capture invisible.
impact: `v6y fix` refuses to edit after a branch switch ('file changed since the snapshot'); with --changed/--base, issues from 'stale' snapshots are silently dropped (skippedStale), so a cached or committed snapshot set makes `v6y check` pass without checking anything. This is the backbone of CI/fix/agents, and it is heuristic.
fix: Record per-file content hashes at report time on the host (the Metro middleware and the Jest matcher both can read the files listed by sourceFiles(root)) as `files: { 'src/X.tsx': 'sha1' }` in the snapshot, and compare hashes; fall back to mtime only for snapshots without `files`. Treat equal hashes as fresh regardless of time.

title: The snapshot format has no version, provenance or pruning, yet is the shared contract for check, fix, the Action, the MCP server and the pre-commit hook
claim: ScreenSnapshot carries screen/platform/window/capturedAt/root only; isSnapshot() accepts anything with a string screen and root.children; nothing records whether a file came from a device or a test, which v6y version wrote it, or which git state it reflects, and nothing ever removes old files from .v6y/snapshots.
evidence: types.ts:113-120; cli/index.ts:86-89 (isSnapshot), 201-206 (handleReport writes `<screen>.<platform>.json` with no provenance); jest.ts:112-118 writes the same directory with a different sanitiser (slice(0,120)); showcase.test.tsx:152 uses a third naming scheme. `v6y check .v6y/snapshots/*.json` (README:214) re-audits every file forever.
impact: Renamed or deleted screens keep failing CI from leftover files; device captures from last week mix with today's test captures with no way to tell them apart; any future change to A11yNode breaks old files with a confusing error or, worse, wrong results.
fix: Add `version: 1`, `origin: 'app' | 'test'`, `v6y: <pkg version>` and `files` (hashes) to ScreenSnapshot; validate `version` in isSnapshot with an upgrade path; write test and app captures to separate subdirectories; make `check` warn when a snapshot's source files no longer exist and add `v6y snapshots prune` (or prune on write by origin+screen).

title: Snapshot location is hard-coded in four consumers but opt-in for the producer, and `check`/`fix` have no default and no glob expansion
claim: Jest only records when V6Y_SNAPSHOTS is set, while the MCP server, the Action, the Claude hook and the README all assume .v6y/snapshots; `v6y check`/`fix` error out without explicit paths and rely on the shell to expand `*.json`.
evidence: jest.ts:113-114 (`if (!dir) return`); mcp.ts:13 DEFAULT_SNAPSHOTS; action.yml:9 default glob; integrations/claude-code/hooks/pre-commit-check.mjs builds the path itself; bin.ts:40-42 and :61-63 require positionals; mcp.ts:75-99 has expandGlob but bin.ts does not use it; README:185,200.
impact: Forgetting the env var in CI yields a 'No snapshots matched' warning and a green build (action.yml exits 0); on Windows cmd.exe the literal `*.json` reaches fs.readFileSync and the command fails; every integration re-implements the default path.
fix: Record to .v6y/snapshots by default in the matcher (V6Y_SNAPSHOTS=0 to disable, a path to override, or `snapshots.dir` in v6y.config.ts); default `check`/`fix` to .v6y/snapshots/**/*.json when no positional is given; run positionals through expandGlob in bin.ts.

title: `v6y` re-exports all 53 symbols of core, including the docs renderer, colour math, tree helpers and each rule object
claim: The public `v6y` entry is `export *` of nine modules, so parseColor, effectiveBackground, describeNode, defineRule, meaninglessLabelReason, suggestTextColor, RULE_EXAMPLES, renderRuleDocs, globToRegExp and an `audit` alias of auditScreen are all 1.0 API, while README:223 describes it as 'defineConfig, the rules, presets and audit engine'.
evidence: core/src/index.ts:1-9; probe `Object.keys(require('packages/v6y/dist/core/index.js'))` lists 53 exports. defineRule is exported but RuleOptionsMap/RuleId (rules/index.ts:27-42) and resolveConfig (config.ts:144-147) reject any rule id not in the built-in list, so custom rules are not actually possible. dist/core/docs.js + rules/examples.js (12K) ride along into any app that imports v6y/react-native (index.tsx:2 imports @v6y/core). packages/v6y/package.json has no `exports` map, so dist/cli/mcp etc. are importable too.
impact: Renaming any helper becomes a breaking change; users and agents discover defineRule and build on a feature that does not exist; the docs generator ships in app bundles.
fix: Curate index.ts to the intended surface (defineConfig, V6yConfig, presets, allRules/rulesById, auditScreen, groupIssues, shouldFail, resolveConfig, the snapshot/issue types); move docs.ts and examples.ts behind an internal entry used only by scripts/gen-docs.mjs; delete the `audit` alias; add an `exports` map to packages/v6y/package.json listing `.`, `./metro`, `./react-native`, `./babel`, `./jest`, `./auto`, `./project-config`.

title: Five workspace packages plus a hand-rolled bundler exist only to produce one published package
claim: The @v6y/* packages are never published, the split forces a 90-line script that rewrites compiled output and user-facing strings with regexes, the internal dependency graph is layered wrongly (the RN runtime package depends on the Node CLI package), and tests already erase the boundary with aliases.
evidence: root package.json workspaces + build script; bundle.mjs:18-25 TEXT map rewrites '@v6y/core' -> 'v6y' inside any string of any .js/.d.ts, :44-66 regex-rewrites specifiers, :77-87 a leak scan, guarded by packages/v6y/test/bundle.test.ts; packages/react-native/package.json depends on @v6y/cli (for jest.ts:19 formatIssues/CONFIG_FILES); none of packages/*/package.json is `private` and they are 0.0.1 while v6y is 0.1.0; vitest.config.mts:6-11 aliases @v6y/* straight to src; commit cd102a4 'Not published to npm yet'. 5.6k lines of source in total.
impact: Every message, template or specifier that mentions a package name must survive textual rewriting (bundle.test.ts exists because this already broke); five tsconfigs/tsbuildinfos and project references for a small codebase; an accidental `npm publish` inside a workspace would publish @v6y/core@0.0.1.
fix: Collapse to a single package `v6y`: src/{core,babel,metro,react-native,cli}, one tsconfig emitting dist/, the existing root shims (or an exports map), tests importing from ../src. Delete bundle.mjs and the leak test. If the split must stay, set `private: true` on the workspace packages, align versions, and move the Jest matcher's formatting dependency out of the RN package.

title: Jest touch-target frames treat minWidth/minHeight as the element size
claim: measureFromStyle uses `style.width ?? style.minWidth` and `style.height ?? style.minHeight` as the frame, but a minimum is a floor, not a size, so a control with minWidth/minHeight below 24 is reported as that small even when its content makes it large.
evidence: collect.ts:408-413; probe: measureFromStyle({ props: { style: { minWidth: 10, minHeight: 10, paddingHorizontal: 20 } } }) -> {width:10,height:10}; padding-only styles return undefined (skipped). REPORT.md section 6 item 12: only 9% of Bluesky's interactive nodes had explicit sizes, so the rule is mostly blind in Jest while `recommended` keeps it at 'error'.
impact: Test-only false positives on min-sized buttons, and a green Jest run says almost nothing about targets while README:73 frames it as a minor limit.
fix: Accept only numeric width/height; treat minWidth/minHeight >= the configured minimum as 'passes', otherwise unmeasured. Have the matcher report how many interactive nodes had no frame (e.g. '12 of 14 controls unmeasured; run on a device for touch targets') so the gap is visible.

title: Contrast ignores `opacity`, which the collector records but no rule reads
claim: text-contrast composites translucent background colours but applies no `opacity` from the text node or its ancestors, so muted text implemented as opacity passes at full contrast; NodeStyle.opacity is dead data.
evidence: collect.ts:98 stores flat.opacity; types.ts:49; grep of packages/core/src for 'opacity' matches only types.ts; effectiveTextColor/effectiveBackground (tree.ts:65-90) and the rule (visual.ts:103-131) never consult it. README:~165 promises contrast 'computed from styles, compositing translucent backgrounds'.
impact: False negatives for a very common pattern (`opacity: 0.5` secondary text, disabled-looking rows that are not disabled) on device and in tests alike.
fix: Multiply the text colour's alpha by the product of `opacity` on the node and every ancestor up to the opaque background layer, then blend as today; apply the same factor to translucent background layers. If this is out of scope, drop `opacity` from the snapshot before versioning the format.

title: Config validation accepts unknown top-level keys despite the README's 'unknown option fails' promise
claim: resolveConfig validates preset names, rule ids, levels and rule options, but silently ignores unknown top-level keys and unknown keys inside screens/hostTypes/capture, so JS/JSON configs with typos do nothing.
evidence: config.ts:127-186 reads only known properties; probe: resolveConfig({ screen: { ignore: ['dev-menu'] }, rule: { 'missing-label': 'off' }, designsystem: [...] }) returns screenIgnore [], missing-label still on, designSystem [] with no error. README (Configuration section) states 'A typo ... or an unknown option fails with a list of valid choices'. TS users get excess-property checks from defineConfig; .js/.mjs/.cjs/.json users (README:~129 says these 'work too') do not.
impact: A mistyped `screen:`/`rule:`/`designsystem:` silently turns the feature off; the failure surfaces as 'v6y does not respect my config'.
fix: Whitelist top-level and nested keys in resolveConfig and throw ConfigError with the known keys, mirroring the rule-option message.

title: Runtime settings are split arbitrarily between v6y.config.ts and an undocumented configure()/provider props
claim: capture.delayMs/pollMs are runtime-only knobs stored in the shared config, while endpoint/log/report/autoCapture/collect are RuntimeOptions only reachable through configure() or <V6yProvider> props, neither of which the README documents; the Jest path needs them (the showcase calls configure() and re-implements measureFromStyle because it is not exported).
evidence: config.ts:35-40 vs index.tsx:14-26 ('Runtime-only settings (not part of v6y.config.ts)'); index.tsx:40-49 configure(); README:225 lists only V6yProvider/capture/trackNavigation; examples/expo-app/src/__tests__/showcase.test.tsx:50-57 duplicates measureFromStyle and calls configure(config, { collect, report: false, log: false, autoCapture: false }); index.tsx:5 exports collect/defaultMeasure/flattenStyle/focusedRouteName/parseSource but not measureFromStyle.
impact: Users of the zero-config path cannot change the endpoint or logging; anyone rendering with V6yProvider in Jest has to copy internal code; the public RN surface mixes internals (collect, parseSource, flattenStyle, getConfig, devServerEndpoint) with the real API.
fix: Put all dev-time settings in one `dev` (or `runtime`) section of V6yConfig read by v6y/auto and the provider; make the matcher/provider detect Jest (JEST_WORKER_ID) and pick measureFromStyle, report:false automatically; trim v6y/react-native exports to V6yProvider, capture, configure (documented) and types.

title: Two screen-change mechanisms coexist: 1 s whole-fiber-tree polling in V6yProvider and an opt-in trackNavigation() that cannot be used from the zero-config path
claim: startWatching walks the entire fiber tree every pollMs to find the focused route, and trackNavigation(ref) only adds an earlier trigger while polling keeps running (both write the module-level lastScreen); the auto path has no navigation ref, so the API is redundant for most users and still costs a tree walk per second.
evidence: index.tsx:106-122 (setInterval + focusedRouteName over the whole tree, collect.ts:229-258), index.tsx:196-212 (trackNavigation shares lastScreen, no way to stop polling), auto.ts installs the provider with defaults. The Bluesky field test rendered trees with hundreds of composites per screen.
impact: API surface users must choose between without guidance; dev-mode CPU cost on large apps; `pollMs` exists only to tune a mechanism that should be event-driven.
fix: Remove trackNavigation from the public API, or make it the provider's own mechanism: find the NavigationContainer ref/context in the tree once and subscribe to its 'state' event, polling only as fallback with `pollMs: 0` to disable.

title: react-test-renderer and @babel/core are required at runtime but not declared as (optional) peers
claim: expect(<El/>).toBeAccessible() requires react-test-renderer and v6y fix / v6y/babel require @babel/core from the project, but the published package only declares react and react-native as optional peers.
evidence: jest.ts:58 require('react-test-renderer'); fix.ts:91-99 loadBabel via createRequire(cwd/package.json); packages/babel-plugin/package.json declares @babel/core as a peer but the bundle (packages/v6y/package.json:15-16) does not; grep of packages/v6y/package.json for babel/react-test-renderer/engines finds nothing. The example pins react-test-renderer 19.3.0 explicitly; React 19 deprecates it.
impact: RNTL-only projects on React 19 hit a module-not-found inside the matcher; install tooling cannot warn; `v6y fix` fails in projects where @babel/core is only transitively present.
fix: Declare @babel/core and react-test-renderer as optional peers with peerDependenciesMeta, prefer @testing-library/react-native's render when it is installed for the element form, and add an `engines.node` field (TS config loading needs >= 22.18).

title: README status, command list and entry-point table are stale
claim: The Status section says the runtime is 'not yet verified on a real simulator or device' and lists 'run on a simulator' and 'a single v6y npm package' as next steps, while the git history records both as done; the command table omits fix and mcp; configure() and V6Y_DISABLE are undocumented.
evidence: README:247 ('Not yet verified...'), :254 and :258 (next up) versus commit 86e9c23 'Device (Android, Expo Go, new architecture): read the dev server URL via SourceCode.getConstants() (bridgeless)...' and cd102a4 'Ship as one package'; README:228 lists `init`, `rules`, `check` and `dev` only (bin.ts:6-21 has fix and mcp); README:225 omits configure (index.tsx:40); V6Y_DISABLE appears only in metro/src/index.ts:26,84. packages/v6y/README.md is also behind the root README (missing the 'Fix automatically' section) because it is only refreshed by the build.
impact: Adopters reading 'pre-alpha, not verified on device' will not try it, and those who do cannot find fix/mcp or the disable switch.
fix: Rewrite Status with what was verified where (Android Expo Go new-arch, Jest on Bluesky; iOS still unverified if so), remove done items, list all six commands, document V6Y_DISABLE and the runtime options, and keep packages/v6y/README.md out of git entirely (it already is ignored) or regenerate it in CI.

title: v6y init always writes v6y.config.ts, which the CLI can only load on Node >= 22.18
claim: init writes a TypeScript config unconditionally, while loadConfig needs Node's built-in type stripping (22.18+) and otherwise throws; Metro and Jest load the same file fine, so the failure only appears in `v6y check`/`fix`/mcp.
evidence: cli/index.ts:305-310 (fs.writeFileSync('v6y.config.ts')), :35-62 (dynamic import, error 'loading TypeScript configs needs Node 22.18 or newer'); no engines field in packages/v6y/package.json; Expo SDK 52+ and RN 0.76+ still support Node 20.
impact: On Node 20 or 22.0-22.17 the recommended first two commands produce a setup that breaks the third; the error looks unrelated to init.
fix: In init, write v6y.config.ts only when process.versions.node >= 22.18 (and ideally when a tsconfig exists), otherwise v6y.config.mjs with the same template; add `engines.node`.

title: Leftovers from earlier iterations: --json alias, CheckOptions.json, /snapshot route, audit() alias, empty CaptureResult interface
claim: Several redundant spellings survive alongside their replacements and are either undocumented or unused.
evidence: bin.ts:67 accepts --json (absent from HELP, bin.ts:6-21, and README); cli/index.ts:100 CheckOptions.json duplicates format; cli/index.ts:241 accepts POST /snapshot although nothing posts there (initial commit already had both routes; the only test hits it with an invalid body); engine.ts:68-71 `audit()` is a one-line alias of auditScreen used only by tests; index.tsx:28 `interface CaptureResult extends SnapshotReport {}` is an empty alias.
impact: Two ways to spell everything, more surface to document and freeze at 1.0.
fix: Delete --json and CheckOptions.json, the /snapshot route (or all of dev(), see the v6y dev finding), the audit alias (tests use auditScreen(...).issues) and CaptureResult.

title: Host-type knowledge is duplicated between core tree.ts and the collector, with loose regex matching in core
claim: tree.ts keeps its own TEXT_TYPES/INPUT_TYPES/IMAGE_TYPES/SWITCH_TYPES tables (regexes such as /Image|FastImage.../ and /Switch/) as a fallback when `kind` is absent, while collect.ts has the authoritative BUILTIN_KINDS list the config `hostTypes` extends; the two already differ (AndroidText only in core).
evidence: tree.ts:4-9,11-27 vs collect.ts:30-36; hasIntrinsicRole (tree.ts:25-27) matches any host whose name contains 'Switch' or 'Slider'; isImage falls back to a substring regex.
impact: Two places to update per new host type; a custom native view named e.g. 'SwitchRowView' silently loses missing-label/missing-role coverage; hostTypes cannot add switch/slider kinds at all.
fix: Move one exact-match table (text, image, input, modal, switch, slider) into core, have the collector import it and extend it with hostTypes, and drop the regex fallbacks.

title: v6y/jest advertises Vitest support but auto-registers only on a global expect and types only jest.Matchers
claim: Registration happens via globalThis.expect?.extend at import time and the type augmentation targets the `jest` namespace, so in Vitest (no globals by default, different Assertion interface) the documented one-line setup neither registers nor types the matcher.
evidence: jest.ts:143-155; README:227 'for Jest and Vitest'; the package's own Vitest test registers manually with expect.extend(matchers) (packages/react-native/test/jest-matcher.test.tsx:7).
impact: Vitest users get 'toBeAccessible is not a function' and no types.
fix: Document `import { matchers } from 'v6y/jest'; expect.extend(matchers)` for Vitest and add `declare module 'vitest' { interface Assertion<T> { toBeAccessible(options?): Promise<void> } }` next to the jest augmentation.

title: v6y fix applies accessibilityRole="button" to every missing-role issue, which is a judgment call for links, tabs and menu items
claim: planEdit maps missing-role unconditionally to add-attr accessibilityRole="button" although the rule's own fix text offers link/tab/checkbox and README:96 promises fixes 'that need no judgment'.
evidence: fix.ts:70-71; roles.ts:21 ('or "link", "tab", "checkbox"'); README:96.
impact: Pressable Text used as a link, tab items and menu rows get announced as buttons after an automated run, which reviewers may not notice in a large diff.
fix: Auto-fix only when the element is a Pressable/Touchable* wrapping non-link content; route Text-with-onPress and elements inside tab bars/menus to the manual list (or choose 'link' for Text with onPress).

title: Snapshot fields that are collected but never consumed: hint, state.expanded/busy, window.fontScale
claim: The collector writes hint, expanded, busy and window.fontScale into every snapshot, but no rule or CLI path reads them.
evidence: types.ts:40-41,67,117; collect.ts:304,111-119; index.tsx:146; grep of packages/core/src for '.hint', 'expanded', 'busy', 'fontScale', '.window' outside types.ts returns nothing.
impact: Noise in a format that is about to be frozen; fontScale in particular is what the planned 200% check (README:257) would need but nothing uses it.
fix: Either use them (fontScale for the font-scale check, hint for a 'hint repeats label' rule) or drop them before adding `version` to the snapshot.

title: Published dist ships source maps whose `sources` point at ../src files that are not in the package
claim: bundle.mjs copies every dist file except .tsbuildinfo, so *.js.map files referencing ../src/*.ts are published while src/ is not, giving broken maps in users' stack traces and bundlers.
evidence: bundle.mjs:31 filter excludes only .tsbuildinfo; packages/v6y/package.json files: ['dist', ...]; head of dist/core/engine.js.map shows "sources":["../src/engine.ts"].
impact: Metro/Jest print warnings about missing sources or map to nothing; extra package weight.
fix: Exclude .map files in the copy filter (or set sourceMap:false for the publish build), or inline sources with inlineSources.

title: Unauthenticated out-of-project file write on the Metro dev server / `v6y dev` via unsanitized snapshot.platform
claim: handleReport sanitizes snapshot.screen with replace(/[^\w.-]+/g,'_') but interpolates snapshot.platform into the output filename unsanitized, so a POSTed snapshot with platform containing '../' writes its JSON file to an arbitrary path outside .v6y/snapshots and outside the project.
evidence: Line 206: fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, `${safe}.${snapshot.platform}.json`), ...). isSnapshot()/snapshotFrom() (index.ts:86-96) and readReport (index.ts:213-232) never validate platform. I called the built handleReport({snapshot:{screen:'Home',platform:'../../written-outside-snapshots-dir',root:{children:[]}}, issues:[], suppressed:[]}, {cwd: proj}) and the file was written to proj's PARENT directory (probeA/written-outside-snapshots-dir.json), outside both .v6y/snapshots and the project dir. This sink is reached with no authentication by the Metro middleware (packages/metro/src/index.ts:130-141 `receive`) and `v6y dev` (index.ts:235-262) on any POST to /v6y/report; neither checks Origin/Host, so any device on the LAN -- or a malicious web page the developer has open, via a no-preflight text/plain POST that the server JSON.parses regardless of content-type -- can trigger it while the dev server runs. Content written is JSON.stringify of the attacker's snapshot (attacker-controlled JSON), extension forced to .json.
impact: A network- or CSRF-reachable primitive to write attacker-chosen JSON to attacker-chosen paths during normal development. Overwriting a .json the toolchain reads (package.json, app.json, tsconfig.json, .vscode/*.json, firebase.json, eslint config) corrupts the project or can chain to code execution. Default-on for every user who adds withV6y(), which is the advertised one-line setup.
fix: Sanitize platform the same way as screen (or hard-restrict to an enum ios|android|unknown), and after building the path assert the resolved target stays within outDir (path.resolve(outDir, name) and check it startsWith(outDir + path.sep)). Apply the same platform sanitization in packages/react-native/src/jest.ts:117 (record()), which has the identical `${name}.${snapshot.platform}.json` pattern. Separately, bind the dev server to localhost by default and/or require a token, and validate the Host header (see the dev-server hardening finding).

title: `v6y fix` writes outside the project via path traversal in snapshot source.file
claim: fix resolves each edit target as path.join(cwd, issue.source.file) with no check that the result stays inside cwd, so a crafted snapshot whose node.source.file contains '../' makes `v6y fix` read and overwrite a file outside the project.
evidence: fix.ts:212 `const abs = path.join(cwd, issue.source.file)`, :231 `fs.readFileSync(abs)`, :235 `fs.writeFileSync(abs, text)`. source.file flows unmodified from the snapshot JSON (engine.ts toIssue copies node.source). I verified path.join('/home/dev/app','../../../../../../tmp/other.tsx') === '/tmp/other.tsx'. The staleness guard (fix.ts:213,218) compares file mtime against the snapshot's own capturedAt, which is attacker-controlled: set it far in the future, or omit it so Number.isNaN(taken) skips the check (fix.ts:218). An interactive node with no role yields a missing-role edit (planEdit, add accessibilityRole="button"), so the attacker can force an applicable edit. The write only lands if the target parses as TS+JSX and has a JSXOpeningElement at the given line:col (applyToFile/findOpening), which constrains WHICH external files can be modified, but the read (readFileSync) and stat happen for any existing path.
impact: Delivery is realistic for the stated goal of repo-committed snapshots: clone or open a repo that ships a malicious .v6y/snapshots/*.json, then `v6y fix` (or the fix_accessibility MCP tool an agent calls by default, with projectDir pointing at that repo) edits files outside the repo (another checkout, a dotfile that is valid JSX/TS). Lower than the dev-server write because it needs the snapshot into the fix input and the external target must be JSX-parseable.
fix: After path.join(cwd, source.file), resolve and assert containment within cwd before any read/write (reject paths that escape). Do the same for the stat in analyze/changed (coverage()). Do not trust capturedAt from the snapshot as the staleness baseline for files outside the snapshot's own directory.

title: Dev-server report endpoint is unauthenticated with no Host/Origin check and no request body size limit
claim: readReport accumulates the POST body with `body += chunk` with no size cap, and the dev/Metro endpoints accept any POST to /v6y/report with no auth and no Host/Origin validation, so an unauthenticated client can exhaust memory and reach the report-handling side effects.
evidence: index.ts:217 `req.on('data', (chunk) => (body += chunk))` -- unbounded; the growth happens in the data handler, outside the try/catch, so a multi-hundred-MB upload drives Metro toward OOM or an unhandled string-length RangeError. dev() (index.ts:235-262) and the Metro middleware (metro/src/index.ts:118-124) gate only on method+url, never on Host/Origin, and Metro/Expo bind to the LAN so devices can connect. readReport (index.ts:224) also returns `data as SnapshotReport` verbatim when the body has an issues[] array, so the saved snapshot and the issue text printed in the Metro terminal are attacker-supplied, not re-audited (log injection into the dev terminal).
impact: Any LAN device or a CSRF/DNS-rebinding page can crash or wedge the developer's Metro process and inject arbitrary text into the Metro terminal. This is the same unauthenticated surface that the platform-traversal write rides on.
fix: Cap the body (reject once body length exceeds e.g. 8-16MB, destroy the socket). Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default (or require a shared token the app reads from the bundle URL). Validate the Host header against localhost/loopback to defeat DNS rebinding. Consider re-auditing client-supplied snapshots rather than trusting a client issues[] array for what gets printed/saved.

title: globToRegExp has catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS)
claim: globToRegExp translates `**` not followed by `/` to `.*`, so a glob with several such segments compiles to a regex with adjacent unbounded quantifiers that backtracks catastrophically against a non-matching path.
evidence: config.ts:196 `re += slash ? '(?:.*/)?' : '.*'`. Measured against the built core: glob = N '**' segments joined by '/', tested on 'a/'.repeat(40)+'b' -> N=5: 19ms, N=10: 117493ms (~2 minutes, process had to be killed). These globs come from v6y.config.ts (ignore, designSystem, screens.ignore -> resolveConfig maps them through globToRegExp and .test()s them against every node's source.file) and from the MCP/CLI snapshots argument (expandGlob .test()s every walked filename).
impact: A mistaken or hostile glob (e.g. committed v6y.config in a shared repo, or a snapshots pattern passed to the MCP tool) hangs `v6y check`, CI, the dev server (loadConfig runs per request), and the MCP server with unbounded CPU. Self-inflicted in the common case, but it is a shipped utility that silently converts a small glob into a DoS.
fix: Collapse consecutive '*'/'**' in the output, avoid emitting adjacent '.*', anchor segments, and/or use a vetted matcher (picomatch/minimatch) instead of a hand-rolled translation. Add a unit test with a pathological glob and a timeout.

title: Pre-commit accessibility gate silently skips `git -c ...` and `git -C ...` commit invocations
claim: The regex that detects `git commit` only allows option tokens of the form `-x` between `git` and `commit`, so `git -c user.email=t@t commit` and `git -C subdir commit` do not match and the gate does nothing for them.
evidence: pre-commit-check.mjs:18 `/(^|[;&|\s(])git\s+(-[^\s]+\s+)*commit(\s|$)/`. The `(-[^\s]+\s+)*` group matches `-c ` or `-C ` but then the NEXT token is the value (`user.email=t@t` / `subdir`), which is neither `-...` nor `commit`, so the match fails. Verified: 'git commit -m x' -> BLOCKED; 'git -c user.email=t@t commit -m x' -> PASSES; 'git -C sub commit' -> PASSES. Note the repo's own tests (cli/test/mcp.test.ts) commit with exactly `git -c user.email=... -c user.name=... commit`.
impact: The plugin's advertised commit gate ('Before Claude runs git commit, the staged files are checked') gives false assurance: Claude committing via the very common `git -c user.email=... commit` form bypasses the a11y check with no indication. A safety feature that is quietly inactive for standard invocations is worse than none.
fix: Match git subcommands robustly: allow option-with-value tokens (`-[cC]\s+\S+`), or tokenize the command and find the first non-option argument after `git` (handling `-c k=v`, `-C dir`, `--git-dir=...`), or detect `commit` as any standalone token after `git`. Add tests for `-c`, `-C`, `--git-dir`.

title: expandGlob reads through symlinked snapshot files
claim: expandGlob does not recurse into symlinked directories (good) but includes symlinked files that match the pattern, which are then opened with readFileSync following the link.
evidence: mcp.ts:92 `if (e.isDirectory()) walk(full)` -- with withFileTypes, a symlink's Dirent.isDirectory() is false, so symlinked dirs are not traversed (verified: linkdir isDirectory=false). A symlink-to-file falls to the else at :94 and is pushed if it matches. Verified: expandGlob('**/*.json', dir) returned both the real file and a symlink 'linkfile.json'. analyze()/fix() then readFileSync that path, following the link.
impact: Minor: a repo could place a symlink in .v6y/snapshots pointing at a file elsewhere; `v6y check`/`fix`/the MCP tools would read it as a snapshot. Low on its own; mainly compounds the fix traversal finding. Directory-symlink traversal is NOT a risk here.
fix: If reading snapshots from untrusted trees matters, lstat matched files and skip symlinks (or resolve and confine within the project root).

title: Published Action/README point consumers at a mutable ref and set no token permissions
claim: The documented CI usage pins the third-party action to a moving branch (`walmat/v6y@main`) and neither the example workflow nor the repo CI sets `permissions:`, so consumers run whatever @main becomes with the repo's default GITHUB_TOKEN scopes.
evidence: README.md:201 `- uses: walmat/v6y@main`. .github/workflows/ci.yml declares no `permissions:` block (defaults to repo setting, often read/write). action.yml is a composite that only emits annotations, so it needs contents: read only. The internal CI also pins actions/checkout@v5 and actions/setup-node@v5 to major tags rather than commit SHAs.
impact: If the repo or a tag is compromised, every consumer pulling @main executes the malicious action with their token. No least-privilege boundary. Standard supply-chain hygiene gap for a tool meant for wide adoption.
fix: Tell users to pin to a release tag or SHA (`walmat/v6y@v1` / @<sha>), publish immutable tags, add `permissions: { contents: read }` to the documented workflow and to ci.yml, and SHA-pin third-party actions. Consider enabling npm provenance when publishing the package.

title: .mcp.json wraps the server in `sh -c` with `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` interpolated inside double quotes
claim: The MCP command is `sh -c 'cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" && exec npx --no-install v6y mcp'`; the project dir is used inside a shell string, so its safety depends on whether the harness pre-expands ${...} before invoking sh.
evidence: .mcp.json:5. If sh performs the ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} expansion at runtime, the value is not re-evaluated and this is safe. If Claude Code substitutes ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} into the args string before spawning, the value lands inside double quotes where sh still performs command substitution, so a project path containing `$(...)` or backticks would execute. I could not confirm the harness's expansion order from the repo, hence the reduced confidence.
impact: At most, a developer who opens a project whose absolute path contains shell metacharacters could get command execution when the MCP server starts. Narrow and depends on harness semantics.
fix: Avoid sh entirely: use the MCP server's own `cwd` field (Claude Code supports it) with `command: npx`, `args: ["--no-install","v6y","mcp"]`, or pass the directory via environment and have `v6y mcp` chdir (serveMcp already honors CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). That removes the shell from the path.

title: Config loading executes arbitrary project code, including inside the dev-server request path (document it)
claim: loadConfig dynamically imports v6y.config.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}, which runs arbitrary code; this is expected but is invoked per POST by the dev server and by every MCP tool call, and is undocumented as a trust assumption.
evidence: index.ts:47 dynamicImport(pathToFileURL(file)); also createRequire fallback at :51 and JSON at :40. Called by check/analyze, by the Metro middleware `receive` (metro/src/index.ts:132 loadConfig per request -- cached by Node after first import), by `v6y dev` per request, and by MCP callTool via analyze. This is the same trust model as babel.config/metro.config, so it is acceptable, but it means running `v6y` anywhere trusts that project's config code.
impact: No new vulnerability beyond the normal 'config files are code' model, but worth stating so users and CI understand that `v6y check` on an untrusted repo executes that repo's v6y.config.
fix: Document in README/agents.md that v6y.config is executed like any JS config and should only be run on trusted projects; optionally support JSON-only config loading for untrusted/CI contexts.

title: fix writes syntactically broken source when an insertion and a removal land at the same offset
claim: When one element gets an add-attr (inserted at opening.name.end) and a remove-attr whose attribute is the first one (its removal range also starts at opening.name.end), the splices are applied in the wrong order with offsets from the original text, so the removal slices through the just-inserted text and corrupts the file.
evidence: Ran the built fix() on `<Text allowFontScaling={false} onPress={go}>Hi</Text>` with a snapshot node {interactive:true, allowFontScaling:false} (missing-role + font-scaling-disabled). Output file: `<Textn" allowFontScaling={false} onPress={go}>Hi</Text>` and renderFix reported 'Fixed 2 issues'. Line 177 sorts equal-start splices so the insertion precedes the range; line 185 applies them descending by start but the range's `end` is not shifted after the insertion.
impact: v6y fix silently writes a file that no longer parses, while reporting success; the user only finds out at the next build. Any pressable Text whose first attribute is allowFontScaling={false} triggers it.
fix: Apply splices in an order that keeps earlier offsets valid: sort by `b.start - a.start || b.end - a.end` so at an equal start the removal range is applied before the zero-width insertion (then the insertion's offset is still correct); or rebuild the output in one forward pass from the original text. Add a test with a removal and an insertion on the same element.

title: fix edits the element's own source even when v6y attributed the issue to the call site, so fixes land in shared components for every usage
claim: fix() always plans the edit at issue.source (lines 206, 212, 223) and ignores issue.location, issue.via and issue.scope, so a call-site-scoped issue inside a design-system component is 'fixed' inside the shared component, changing every screen that uses it.
evidence: Built a project with shared `AppText(props) => <Text {...props} />` used once as a 24pt title and once as 14pt body text; with `extends: 'strict'` (and again with designSystem: ['src/components/**'], where the engine sets location=Home.tsx:6 via AppText.tsx:3) fix() wrote `<Text accessibilityRole="header" {...props} />` into AppText.tsx and reported it as fixed. Same mechanism for hitSlop: a shared IconButton rendered at 20×20 and 40×40 got one `hitSlop={14}` chosen from whichever issue sorted first (seen-key dedupe at line 137).
impact: Every paragraph rendered through the shared text component becomes a screen-reader heading (no rule detects that, so the next check looks clean); hitSlop/role inserted into shared components affect all call sites, exactly the attribution problem the field test fixed in the engine. On Bluesky this would mark all Typography text as headings.
fix: Respect the engine's attribution: when issue.scope === 'call-site' and issue.via is set (location.file !== source.file), either apply the attribute at issue.location (the JSX call site, which forwards props in the common `{...props}` case) or list it as manual with 'inside shared component X; fix at the call site'. Only edit issue.source when scope === 'component' or location === source. For missing-heading, additionally require the title Text to be written in the screen file itself.

title: Snapshots keyed by screen name only: Home.ios.json and Home.android.json collide in both fix and analyze
claim: fix.ts:199 (`new Map(snapshots.map(s => [s.screen, …]))`) and index.ts:135 (`new Map(cover.stale.map(s => [s.screen, …]))` ) keep only the last snapshot per screen name, but node ids are only stable within one snapshot and staleness is per snapshot, so a second platform's snapshot of the same screen gets the wrong node or the wrong stale set.
evidence: fix(): with Home.ios (node '1' = 20×20 pressable) and Home.android (node '1' = a Text, '2' = the pressable at 48×48), the iOS touch-target issue was reported as 'needs a manual fix [touch-target-size]' instead of 'add hitSlop={14}'; iOS alone produced the hitSlop fix. analyze(): iOS snapshot captured an hour ago (stale), Android an hour ahead (fresh), Home.tsx edited in between: both orders gave issues: 0, skippedStale: 2, failed: false, where the fresh Android error should have been reported. handleReport writes `${screen}.${platform}.json` and jest.ts:117 writes `${name}.${platform}.json`, so jest-expo's universal preset or any ios+android capture produces exactly this pair.
impact: Fixable issues are demoted to manual, hitSlop can be computed from another platform's frame, and errors from a fresh snapshot are silently dropped by `check --changed`, so CI passes.
fix: Key by snapshot identity, not name: have analyze() return issues with a reference/index to their snapshot (or carry `platform` + index), compute `stale` per snapshot object (Map<ScreenSnapshot, Set<string>>), and in fix() look up nodes from the snapshot the issue came from. Add a test with two platforms of one screen.

title: mtime-based staleness makes `check --changed/--base` silently pass in CI checkouts and after formatters
claim: coverage() calls a snapshot stale for a changed file when the file's mtime is newer than capturedAt, and analyze() (index.ts:143-148) then drops every issue touching that file; a git checkout, `prettier --write`, lint --fix or branch switch bumps mtimes without changing the lines, so the gate passes vacuously.
evidence: Repo with .v6y/snapshots/Home.ios.json (capturedAt yesterday, 20×20 button error) committed, PR branch edits Home.tsx: `check([snap], {changed: {base: 'main'}})` printed 'Checking changes since main: 1 changed file, 0 of 0 issues touch them. ✓ No accessibility issues found. ⚠ Snapshot "Home" is older… 1 issue from stale snapshots skipped' and returned exit code 0. Same with --changed after rewriting Home.tsx with identical content plus a comment. README.md:41 tells users the dev server saves snapshots 'for CI', i.e. to commit them; `--format json` (index.ts:182) prints only a.issues, with no trace of skippedStale.
impact: The CI gate and the pre-commit hook report green on a PR that introduces errors whenever the snapshot predates the checkout or a formatter touched the file; the only signal is a yellow warning in text mode and nothing in JSON.
fix: Decide staleness with git rather than mtime: for --base compare capturedAt with `git log -1 --format=%cI <base>..HEAD -- <file>` and for the working tree only consider files `git status --porcelain` lists as modified (or hash the file at capture time in the collector and compare hashes). Until then: never drop issues, only annotate them as 'possibly stale', or make dropping opt-in; include stale/uncovered/skippedStale in the JSON and GitHub outputs; and in CI mode fail (or warn loudly) when every snapshot is stale.

title: A file Babel can't parse (Flow, decorators) aborts the whole fix run after earlier files were already rewritten
claim: applyToFile parses every file with the fixed plugin list ['jsx','typescript'] and does not catch parse errors; fix() writes each file as it goes (line 235), so a later unparseable file throws out of fix(), the CLI prints the Babel error with exit 2, and the files already modified are never reported.
evidence: Snapshot covering src/A.tsx (fixable) and src/B.js with `// @flow` + `type Props = {| go: () => void |}`: fix() threw '…/src/B.js: Unexpected token (3:14)'; A.tsx was changed on disk, B.js untouched, no FixResult returned. A .tsx with `@observer class` threw "Support for the experimental syntax 'decorators' isn't currently enabled". bin.ts:91-94 turns that into 'v6y: … Unexpected token' exit 2.
impact: Users with any Flow-typed .js (the pre-0.71 RN template) or MobX decorators get a crash and silent partial edits in their working tree; the MCP fix_accessibility tool returns only an error text.
fix: Parse per file inside try/catch and push a skipped entry ('could not parse: <babel message>'); choose parser plugins by extension (flow for .js/.jsx with an @flow pragma, typescript otherwise) and add 'decorators-legacy' (or try the project's own Babel config via parseSync with babelrc/configFile enabled first). Plan all files before writing any, so a failure never leaves partial edits unreported.

title: git quotes non-ASCII paths, so issues in those files never match --changed, coverage or staleness
claim: `git diff --name-only` and `git ls-files` are read as text with git's default core.quotePath, so a path with non-ASCII characters arrives as `"src/Caf\303\251.tsx"` (quoted, octal-escaped) and never equals the snapshot's `src/Café.tsx`.
evidence: changedFiles() on a repo with modified src/Café.tsx and untracked src/Ünicode New.tsx returned ["\"src/Caf\\303\\251.tsx\"", "src/My Screen.tsx", "\"src/\\303\\234nicode New.tsx\""]; files.has('src/Café.tsx') === false (spaces alone are fine).
impact: Issues in such files are dropped from `check --changed`, never annotated on PRs, never flagged as stale or uncovered; silent.
fix: Run git with `-z` and split on NUL (`git diff --name-only -z …`, `git ls-files -z …`), or pass `-c core.quotePath=false`; add a test with a non-ASCII filename.

title: loadConfig caches .ts/.js/.mjs configs for the life of the process, so `v6y dev` and the Metro middleware never pick up config edits
claim: The dynamic import() is keyed by file URL, so after the first load every later loadConfig(cwd) call returns the original module; only the .json branch (line 41) re-reads the file. dev() (line 246) and metro's receive() call loadConfig per report expecting fresh config.
evidence: Wrote v6y.config.{mjs,js,ts} with failOn 'never', called loadConfig, rewrote to 'warning', called again: all three returned 'never' (STALE); v6y.config.json returned 'warning'.
impact: Changing a rule level or ignore while the dev server/Metro runs has no effect on server-side audits until restart, and behaviour differs by config file extension; confusing while tuning rules.
fix: Track the config file's mtimeMs and import with a cache-busting query when it changed (`pathToFileURL(file).href + '?v=' + mtimeMs`), or memoise per (file, mtime) explicitly and document that .ts configs reload on change.

title: check/fix neither expand globs nor default to .v6y/snapshots/*.json, so the documented invocation fails on shells that don't expand
claim: Positional arguments are passed straight to fs.readFileSync; a literal `*.json` (cmd.exe, PowerShell, zsh with no match, or a quoted pattern) becomes ENOENT with exit 2, and running `v6y check` with no files is a usage error although mcp.ts already has DEFAULT_SNAPSHOTS and expandGlob().
evidence: `node bin.js check '.v6y/snapshots/*.json'` → 'v6y: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.v6y/snapshots/*.json'' exit 2; `node bin.js check` → usage error exit 2. README and docs/agents.md show the glob form everywhere.
impact: Windows users and anyone quoting the pattern get an opaque ENOENT; every CI/hook snippet must spell the glob.
fix: In bin.ts, expand each positional through expandGlob(pattern, cwd) and default to DEFAULT_SNAPSHOTS when none is given (mirroring the MCP tools and action.yml's default); say 'No snapshots match …' with the recording hint instead of ENOENT.

title: MCP tools default to changed-only and fail with a raw git error in projects that aren't a git repository
claim: check_accessibility defaults changedOnly to true and fix_accessibility passes changed: true unless changedOnly === false, so in a non-git directory both return isError 'v6y: --changed needs a git repository.' with no hint about changedOnly.
evidence: callTool('check_accessibility', {}, <dir with .v6y/snapshots but no .git>) returned {content:[{text:'v6y: --changed needs a git repository.'}], isError:true}.
impact: An agent in a fresh or exported project (or a monorepo subdir it treats as the project) gets an error instead of results and has to guess the parameter; the same happens before the first commit (see the no-HEAD finding).
fix: When git is unavailable or has no HEAD, fall back to all issues and prepend a note ('not a git repository; showing all issues'), and mention changedOnly in the error text; add `base`/`staged` to fix_accessibility to match check_accessibility.

title: missing-role is always auto-fixed as "button", which is wrong for links and masks state-not-exposed on custom toggles
claim: planEdit writes accessibilityRole="button" for every missing-role issue without looking at the node: a Text with onPress (inline link), a navigation link, or a Pressable that already carries accessibilityState.checked/selected (a custom checkbox/switch/tab) all become buttons.
evidence: fix.ts:69-71 has no conditions; roles.ts:63-69 only flags state-not-exposed for roles in STATEFUL (checkbox, switch, radio, togglebutton, tab), so once 'button' is written a toggle that never exposes its state is never reported again. The rule's own message says 'button or link' and its fix text lists checkbox/tab alternatives.
impact: A one-command 'fix' that announces toggles and links as buttons, and hides a real defect from future checks; this is the opposite of the README's 'never guesses' promise.
fix: Only auto-apply 'button' when the node has no state keys (state/droppedState empty) and is not a text node; send nodes with checked/selected/expanded state, and Text-with-onPress, to the manual list with a suggested role ('has checked state: use checkbox or switch'), or pick the role from the state key.

title: --changed in a repo without commits (or --base with an unknown ref) surfaces a raw 'Command failed: git diff … fatal: ambiguous argument' error
claim: The default branch diffs against HEAD and the --base branch falls back to diffing against the ref itself; when HEAD or the ref doesn't exist, execFileSync's error (command line plus git's stderr) is thrown verbatim.
evidence: changedFiles(dir) in a `git init` repo with no commits threw "Command failed: git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=ACMR HEAD | fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision…"; `{base: 'origin/main'}` without a remote threw the same for origin/main. --staged works (empty tree) and the MCP tools and hook hit the HEAD case right after `create-expo-app` + `git init`.
impact: The first run of check --changed, the Claude Code commit gate and check_accessibility in a brand-new project fail with an internal-looking error.
fix: Probe `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` first and, when absent, diff against the empty tree (`git hash-object -t tree /dev/null`) or treat all tracked+untracked files as changed; for --base, verify the ref and say 'unknown ref origin/main: fetch it first (git fetch origin main)'.

title: hitSlop fix targets a hard-coded 48 regardless of the configured touch-target-size options or preset
claim: TARGET = 48 is used for every hitSlop computation, ignoring the resolved rule options (minimum, ios, android, platformGuidelines); the wcag22-aa preset sets platformGuidelines: false (24 minimum) and users can set `minimum: 32`, yet fix inflates every flagged target to 48 and reports '(48pt target on iOS and Android)'.
evidence: fix.ts:44 and planEdit(issue, node, TARGET) at line 206; config.ts:93 (`'touch-target-size': ['error', { platformGuidelines: false }]`); the rule's own fix text (visual.ts:46) computes slop from the platform guide, not 48.
impact: Under a WCAG-only policy a 20×20 target gets hitSlop={14} (48×48) where 24 was required, enlarging touch areas (overlapping neighbours in toolbars) beyond what the team asked for.
fix: Expose the resolved config from analyze() (it already calls resolveConfig) and compute the target from the rule's options: `platformGuidelines ? Math.max(ios, android) : minimum`; mention the target used in the reason string.

title: v6y fix --changed silently drops stale-snapshot issues: skippedStale and stale warnings never reach FixResult
claim: fix() uses analysis.issues but discards analysis.skippedStale and analysis.cover, and renderFix has no field for them, so issues removed by the staleness filter are neither fixed, listed as manual, nor shown as skipped.
evidence: fix.ts:190-239 only reads analysis.issues; FixResult (lines 34-41) has applied/manual/skipped; renderFix (242-267) prints nothing about stale snapshots, whereas renderAnalysis (index.ts:164-171) does.
impact: After editing a screen, `v6y fix --changed` or fix_accessibility prints 'Nothing to fix automatically.' with no explanation, while check --changed warns; agents following the documented loop get contradictory signals.
fix: Carry cover.stale and skippedStale into FixResult (e.g. `stale: Coverage['stale']`, `skippedStale: number`) and print the same 'Snapshot … is older than your edits; re-run its test' lines in renderFix and in the MCP structured output.

title: A parseable non-object line (e.g. `null`) crashes the MCP server; batch arrays are silently dropped
claim: handleMessage dereferences msg.id without checking that msg is an object, and the readline handler in serveMcp has no catch, so a `null` or numeric line raises TypeError in an async handler → unhandled rejection → process exit 1; a JSON array (JSON-RPC batch) has no `id`, is treated as a notification and gets no response.
evidence: Spawned `bin.js mcp`, sent `null` then a ping: process exited code=1 with 'mcp.js:177 if (msg.id === undefined)' on stderr. Sent `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}]`: no response for id 1 (server kept running).
impact: A misbehaving or older client (batching was legal in 2025-03-26) can kill the server or hang waiting for a reply; the agent loses the tool mid-session.
fix: Validate the message shape (object with jsonrpc '2.0'); reply with -32600 Invalid Request (id null) for non-objects and for arrays (or support batches); wrap the per-line handler in try/catch so no exception escapes the readline callback.

title: Removing an attribute on its own line in a CRLF file leaves a lone carriage return
claim: The whitespace walk-back checks for '\n' and then only [ \t], so the '\r' preceding it is kept, producing `<Text\r\r\n      style=…`.
impact: Valid JS but a stray CR that shows as ^M in diffs and trips line-ending linters; Windows checkouts with autocrlf see it on every removal.
fix: Treat '\r\n' as the line break when walking back (if text[start-2..start] === '\r\n' remove both), and add a CRLF test.

title: Attributes are inserted before TypeScript type arguments and on the tag-name line of multi-line elements
claim: Insertion at opening.name.end precedes a generic element's type arguments (Babel 7 stores them in opening.typeParameters), producing invalid JSX, and for prettier-style multi-line openings the new attributes are appended to the `<Pressable` line instead of their own line.
evidence: `<Row<string> onPress={go} items={[]} />` became `<Row accessibilityRole="button" hitSlop={14}<string> onPress…`; Babel 7.29.7 parse shows name.end=4, typeParameters.end=12. A multi-line `<Pressable\n  onPress…` became `<Pressable accessibilityRole="button" hitSlop={14}\n      onPress=…`.
impact: Generic components (rare in RN) get a syntax error; prettier-formatted projects get a diff that lint-staged immediately reformats.
fix: Insert at `(opening.typeParameters ?? opening.typeArguments)?.end ?? opening.name.end`; when the first existing attribute starts on a later line, reuse the text between name.end and that attribute (newline + indent) as the separator so each new attribute gets its own line.

title: MCP conformance gaps: protocolVersion echoed verbatim, protocol errors returned as tool results, text block isn't the structured JSON
claim: initialize returns whatever protocolVersion the client sent (spec: respond with a version the server supports); unknown tools and missing arguments come back as isError tool results instead of -32602 Invalid params; response-shaped messages with an id get -32601; structuredContent is returned without an outputSchema and the accompanying text block is the human report rather than the serialized JSON the spec says SHOULD accompany structured content.
evidence: handleMessage initialize with protocolVersion '2099-12-31' → result.protocolVersion '2099-12-31'; tools/call with no params → {isError:true, text:'Unknown tool "undefined".'}; {id:7, result:{}} → error -32601 'Method not found: undefined'. TOOLS (lines 25-72) define no outputSchema while callTool returns structuredContent (lines 129, 154).
impact: Mostly harmless with current clients (tools-only server), but strict clients may validate the version or expect JSON-RPC errors for bad calls; a wrong version claim is a lie to the client.
fix: Keep a SUPPORTED list ['2025-06-18','2025-03-26','2024-11-05'] and return the requested one if supported else the latest; return -32602 for unknown tool / missing required args; ignore messages carrying result/error; either add outputSchema for the two check/fix tools or put the JSON in a second text block.

title: Flag parsing silently accepts --port=1234, a valueless --base, and unknown flags; --json is undocumented and CheckOptions.json is a leftover
claim: option() only understands `--flag value`, so `--port=1234` is ignored (listens on 8973); `--base` as the last argument yields base undefined and a full audit; a misspelt `--chnaged` is accepted and audits everything; `--json` works but isn't in HELP while CheckOptions.json duplicates format.
evidence: `dev --port=1234` printed 'v6y listening on :8973'; `check snap --base` printed the full report exit 1; `check snap --chnaged` ran a full audit exit 1; `check snap --json` printed JSON. HELP (lines 6-21) lists only --format; index.ts:98-102 has both json and format.
impact: A typo of --changed in a pre-commit hook turns the staged check into a full-repo audit; --port= users are confused by the wrong port.
fix: Parse `--flag=value`, reject unknown flags with the usage text and exit 2, error when a flag that takes a value has none, and either document --json or drop it together with CheckOptions.json.

title: Manual/skipped messages are vague or duplicated and ORDER lists attributes the fixer never inserts
claim: MANUAL_WHY has no entries for touch-target-size (no frame / already has hitSlop) or missing-heading (no title found) so they print 'needs a manual fix'; a font-scaling issue whose allowFontScaling comes from Text.defaultProps or a wrapper prints 'allowFontScaling not found'; 'file not found' is pushed once per issue (duplicates); ORDER (line 172) includes accessibilityLabel and accessibilityState which planEdit never produces.
evidence: Probe output: '• src/Screen.tsx:5  needs a manual fix  [touch-target-size]'; '- src/S.tsx:4  allowFontScaling not found' for a defaultProps case; 'Skipped: - src/Home.tsx:3 file not found' printed twice for one file in `fix --dry-run`.
impact: Polish: the manual list is the hand-off to a person or agent, and these lines don't say what to do.
fix: Add reasons ('no layout frame in this snapshot; run on a device or set width/height', 'already has hitSlop; increase padding', 'allowFontScaling={false} is set elsewhere, e.g. Text.defaultProps or a wrapper'), dedupe skipped by file:line:why, and trim ORDER to the attributes actually inserted.

title: coverage() assumes components are .tsx/.jsx: JS projects never get the uncovered warning and non-screen .tsx files are reported as unrendered
claim: `uncovered` filters changed files by /\.(tsx|jsx)$/ and excludes only test files, so a JS-only RN app (App.js, screens/*.js) is never told a changed screen has no snapshot, while hooks, theme, navigation or icon files ending in .tsx trigger 'No snapshot renders … Open those screens in the app or add a toBeAccessible() test.'
evidence: changed.ts:109; renderAnalysis message at index.ts:170. Field reports show design-system and util .tsx files are the bulk of changed files on a real PR.
impact: Noise on most PRs in TS projects and no coverage signal in JS projects.
fix: Detect JSX-bearing files by content (quick check for '<' + a capitalised tag or a `from 'react-native'` import) rather than extension, or restrict the warning to files under configured screen globs; keep the wording hedged ('may be a screen').

title: init writes a TypeScript config even on Node versions whose CLI can't load it
