claim: init() unconditionally writes v6y.config.ts, but loadConfig needs Node ≥ 22.18 for .ts (the error at line 59 says so), so on Node 20/22.x-older the very next `v6y check` fails with the version error.
evidence: index.ts:305-311 has no version check; README.md:131 documents the Node requirement. Could not reproduce here (Node 24.15.0); reasoning from code.
impact: A two-command quick start fails on still-supported Node 22 minors below .18.
fix: Compare process.versions.node with 22.18 in init() and write v6y.config.mjs (with a comment) or print the requirement before writing; or make loadConfig fall back to transpiling .ts with the project's @babel/core (it's required anyway for fix).

title: Commit gate can be bypassed by common git forms and ignores non-1 exit codes
claim: The command regex only tolerates valueless flags between `git` and `commit`, so `git -c user.name=x commit` and `git -C apps/mobile commit` are not checked; and only `result.status === 1` blocks, so a crash or usage error from `v6y check` (exit 2: invalid config, unreadable snapshot, no HEAD) lets the commit through silently.
evidence: Evaluated the regex: 'git commit -m x' true, 'git -c a=b commit' false, 'git -C apps/mobile commit -m x' false; line 28 checks `result.status === 1` only.
impact: The gate advertised in README/docs/agents.md is weaker than described; failures look like passes.
fix: Match `git` followed by any options (`(?:\s+-\S+(?:\s+\S+)?)*`) then `commit`; treat status 2 as a blocking 'v6y could not run: <stderr>' (or at least warn), and prefer `node_modules/.bin/v6y.cmd` on win32.

title: README's command list omits fix and mcp; fix_accessibility lacks the base/staged inputs check_accessibility has
claim: The 'What's in the package' table says `npx v6y` provides 'the init, rules, check and dev commands' though fix and mcp exist and are documented elsewhere in the same README; the MCP fix tool can't be scoped with base/staged while the check tool and the CLI can.
evidence: README.md:228; mcp.ts:46-55 (fix_accessibility schema: changedOnly, dryRun, snapshots, projectDir only) vs lines 30-40 (check_accessibility adds base, staged); bin.ts:17-18 says fix takes --changed/--staged/--base.
impact: Doc drift and an inconsistent tool surface for agents (check on a branch, then fix can't use the same scope).
fix: Update the table row to 'init, rules, check, fix, dev and mcp'; add base and staged to fix_accessibility and pass them through like check_accessibility does.

title: `--changed`/`--staged`/`--base` silently drop issues in files outside the project directory (monorepo shared packages); GitHub annotations get unnormalized paths
claim: changedFiles() runs `git diff --relative`, which only lists files under cwd, while the Babel plugin stamps files outside the project root as `../../packages/ui/Button.tsx`; touchesChange() therefore never matches an issue in a sibling workspace package, and githubAnnotations() (line 124) emits `file=apps/mobile/../../packages/ui/Button.tsx` without normalizing.
evidence: Reproduced against packages/v6y/dist/cli/index.js in a scratch git repo with apps/mobile and packages/ui, editing both: `prefix: "apps/mobile/" files: ['src/Screen.tsx']`, `sibling package issue touches change? false`, `app issue touches change? true`, annotation `::error file=apps/mobile/../../packages/ui/Button.tsx`. packages/babel-plugin/src/index.ts:95 computes `path.relative(root, filename)` so out-of-root files get `..` segments.
impact: In any Expo/RN monorepo with a shared UI package (the common design-system layout, and exactly what `designSystem` attribution targets), editing the shared component yields no `v6y check --changed` output, no PR annotation and no pre-commit block, while `coverage()` still reports it; users conclude the change is clean.
fix: Diff from the repo root without `--relative` (or keep `--relative` but also run `git diff --name-only` for the whole repo), convert both sides to repo-root-relative POSIX paths: `path.posix.normalize(path.posix.join(prefix, issueFile))` vs `git diff` output, and apply the same normalization in githubAnnotations() before printing `file=`. Add a test with a sibling-package issue.

title: No `exports` map: `v6y/metro`, `v6y/babel`, `v6y/jest`, `v6y/auto` are unresolvable from Node ESM (metro.config.mjs, babel.config.mjs, any ESM script)
claim: The published package relies on root shim files (`metro.js`, `babel.js`, …) with no `exports` field, so Node's ESM resolver, which does not probe extensions for bare subpaths, fails on every subpath import.
evidence: `node --input-type=module -e "import { withV6y } from 'v6y/metro'"` → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module .../node_modules/v6y/metro ... Did you mean to import "file:///.../packages/v6y/metro.js"?` while `import { defineConfig } from 'v6y'` works (main). Metro accepts `metro.config.mjs` (`SEARCH_JS_EXTS = ['.js','.cjs','.mjs','.json']` in examples/expo-app/node_modules/metro-config/src/loadConfig.js:57) and Babel accepts `babel.config.mjs`.
impact: Projects with `"type": "module"` or `.mjs` Metro/Babel configs cannot use `withV6y` or `v6y/babel` without switching to `createRequire`; the error message names a file the user never wrote.
fix: Add an `exports` map covering `.`, `./metro`, `./babel`, `./jest`, `./auto`, `./react-native`, `./project-config` and `./package.json`, each as `{ "types": "./metro.d.ts", "default": "./metro.js" }`; keep `main`/`types` for legacy resolvers. Keep `./project-config` in the map so Metro with `unstable_enablePackageExports` still resolves the empty fallback when `withV6y` is not used. Add a test that imports each subpath from an ESM context.

title: Applying `withV6y` twice makes the transformer require itself and recurse: every file fails with "Maximum call stack size exceeded"
claim: withV6y() unconditionally records `config.transformer.babelTransformerPath` as the upstream; when that path is already v6y's own transformer, the worker's `require(UPSTREAM)` returns its own module, whose hoisted `exports.transform` calls itself.
evidence: Reproduced: `withV6y(withV6y(base))` sets `V6Y_UPSTREAM_TRANSFORMER=/.../packages/v6y/dist/metro/transformer.js`; calling the resulting transformer's `transform()` throws `Maximum call stack size exceeded`. dist/metro/transformer.js lines 7 and 24 show `exports.transform = transform` before `const upstream = require(UPSTREAM)`.
impact: Anyone who wraps twice (a template that already applies withV6y, a config helper, or copy-paste) gets a stack overflow on the first bundle with no mention of v6y; `v6y init` only guards by grepping metro.config.js for `withV6y`.
fix: Make withV6y idempotent: `if (config.transformer?.babelTransformerPath === require.resolve('./transformer')) return config;` and in transformer.ts throw a clear `[v6y] withV6y() was applied twice` when `path.resolve(UPSTREAM) === __filename`. Add a test.

title: No prepublish guard and the generated README is already stale; version lives in three places; no tags; action pinned to `@main`
claim: Nothing ties `npm publish` to a fresh build: `packages/v6y/README.md` is gitignored and only refreshed by bundle.mjs, and the copy on disk right now lacks the `## Fix automatically` section that the root README has, so a publish without rebuilding ships stale docs (and potentially stale dist).
evidence: `diff README.md packages/v6y/README.md` shows lines 75-97 (`## Fix automatically` …) missing; `npm pack --dry-run` lists README.md at 11.6 kB vs 12.9 kB at the root. No `prepublishOnly`/`prepack` in packages/v6y/package.json or the root package.json; `git tag` is empty; versions: packages/v6y 0.1.0, integrations/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json 0.1.0, five workspace packages 0.0.1 with exact pins (packages/metro/package.json:8-12); README.md:201 tells users `uses: walmat/v6y@main`; `scripts.bundle` points at scripts/bundle.mjs which `files` excludes; no `repository.directory`.
impact: First release is one forgotten `npm run build` away from publishing the wrong README or an outdated dist, bumps must be edited by hand in several files, and the Action has no stable ref for users to pin.
fix: Add `"prepack": "cd ../.. && npm run build && npx vitest run"` to packages/v6y (or a release workflow that runs `npm test` then `npm publish --provenance` from packages/v6y), derive plugin.json's version from packages/v6y/package.json in bundle.mjs, tag releases `vX.Y.Z` plus a floating `v0` for the Action and document `uses: walmat/v6y@v0`, add `"repository": { "directory": "packages/v6y" }`, drop the `bundle` script from the published package.json.

title: `v6y/jest` requires `react-test-renderer` at runtime but no package declares it
claim: The element form `await expect(<X/>).toBeAccessible()` does `require('react-test-renderer')`, yet packages/v6y/package.json lists only `react` and `react-native` as (optional) peers; projects without react-test-renderer get a bare module-not-found error.
evidence: jest.ts:57-64 `renderElement` requires 'react-test-renderer'; packages/v6y/package.json peerDependencies = react, react-native; packages/react-native/package.json likewise. React Native Testing Library v13+ no longer depends on react-test-renderer and React 19 deprecates it (not re-verified here).
impact: The README's `await expect(<Checkout />).toBeAccessible()` fails with `Cannot find module 'react-test-renderer'` in RNTL 13 projects, with no hint that the render-result form works.
fix: Declare `react-test-renderer` in peerDependencies with `peerDependenciesMeta.optional: true`; wrap the require and throw `v6y: rendering a bare element needs react-test-renderer; pass render(<X/>) from @testing-library/react-native instead`; consider using RNTL's `render` when it is resolvable.

title: bundle.mjs and gen-docs.mjs break on Windows and on checkout paths containing spaces (`import.meta.url` pathname used as a filesystem path)
claim: `path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname)` yields `/C:/…` on Windows and percent-encoded segments (`My%20Code`) everywhere, so `fs.existsSync(src)` fails and the build aborts with `missing …/dist: run the workspace build first`; scripts/gen-docs.mjs:6 has the same bug. Additionally `rel()` (line 36) uses `path.relative`, which on Windows writes backslash specifiers like `require("..\\core\\index.js")` into files Metro later bundles.
evidence: Read bundle.mjs:8-11,35-39 and gen-docs.mjs:6; `new URL(...).pathname` percent-encodes and keeps the leading slash before the drive letter (Node behaviour, not reproduced on Windows here). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs ubuntu only, so neither case is exercised.
impact: Contributors on Windows, or anyone with a space in the repo path, cannot run `npm run build`/`npm test`/`npm run docs`; a Windows-built tarball would carry unresolvable specifiers.
fix: Use `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` (or `import.meta.dirname`, Node ≥20.11) in both scripts, and make `rel()` return POSIX separators: `.split(path.sep).join('/')`. Add a windows-latest job to CI.

title: Shipped source maps are dangling: `sources` point at `../src/*.ts` that is not published, no `sourcesContent`; 41% of dist by size
claim: Every `*.js.map` in the tarball references `../src/index.ts` relative to `dist/<part>/`, a path that does not exist in the published package, and `sourcesContent` is absent, so the maps resolve to nothing while adding 137,606 of 334,438 bytes to dist.
evidence: packages/v6y/dist/core/index.js.map: `"sources":["../src/index.ts"]`, no `sourcesContent`; measured map share = 41%; `npm pack --dry-run` lists all 27 maps; tsconfig.base.json has `sourceMap: true` without `inlineSources`.
impact: Stack traces in Metro/Jest point into v6y with unresolvable original positions; package is ~40% larger than needed.
fix: Either set `"inlineSources": true` (so maps carry the TS source and help users read Metro stack traces) or exclude `**/*.map` and strip `//# sourceMappingURL` comments in bundle.mjs.

title: Internal workspace packages are publishable and over-specified: not `private`, exact `0.0.1` cross-pins, and an unused peer dependency
claim: `@v6y/core`, `@v6y/cli`, `@v6y/babel-plugin`, `@v6y/metro`, `@v6y/react-native` lack `"private": true`, so `npm publish --workspaces` or a publish from a package dir would push packages the product does not want on npm; `@v6y/metro` pins its siblings to exactly `0.0.1` and declares a peer on `@v6y/react-native` it never imports.
evidence: Read all five packages/*/package.json; only the root package.json is private; packages/metro/src/*.ts import `@v6y/cli` and `@v6y/babel-plugin` only (the react-native import is a string in transformer.ts:23).
impact: Accidental publish of five extra packages with inconsistent versions; version bumps need edits in five files.
fix: Add `"private": true` to the five internal packages, replace exact pins with `"*"` (workspace-only), remove the `@v6y/react-native` peer from packages/metro.

title: Babel plugin: `// v6y-ignore` above `const A = () => <View />` is silently ignored
claim: When the JSX's parent is an ArrowFunctionExpression, findIgnore() reads the arrow's own `leadingComments` instead of the enclosing VariableDeclaration's, so the comment on the line above a `const Component = () => <JSX/>` is never found.
evidence: Reproduced with the bundled plugin: input `// v6y-ignore\nconst A = () => <View />;` → output `<View __v6y="src/A.tsx:2:17" />` with no `__v6yIgnore`; the documented `return` form (README.md:158-159) works.
impact: A common component style gets no suppression and no warning; users assume the comment syntax is broken.
fix: In findIgnore(), when `up.isArrowFunctionExpression()` and `up.parentPath?.isVariableDeclarator()`, take `up.parentPath.parentPath` (the VariableDeclaration) as `stmt`; add a test for the arrow form.

title: Babel plugin stamps intrinsic DOM tags and React built-ins (`Ctx.Provider`, `Suspense`), leaking `__v6y`/`__v6yIgnore` into DOM attributes
claim: Only `Fragment`/`React.Fragment` and namespaced names are skipped; lowercase tags and context providers receive the props, so in Expo DOM components (`'use dom'`) or RN-web files with raw DOM elements `__v6y` becomes a real DOM attribute and the camelCase `__v6yIgnore` triggers React DOM's unknown-prop warning in dev.
evidence: Reproduced with the bundled plugin: `<Ctx.Provider value={1} __v6y="src/A.tsx:1:17"><div __v6y="src/A.tsx:1:41">…<span __v6y="src/A.tsx:1:64" __v6yIgnore="{\"rules\":\"*\"}" />`. The React DOM warning behaviour for camelCase unknown props is from knowledge, not re-run here.
impact: Noise in the dev console and stray attributes in the DOM for Expo DOM / web code that goes through the same Metro transformer.
fix: Skip names starting with a lowercase letter (intrinsic elements) and extend SKIP with `Suspense`, `StrictMode`, `Profiler` and any `*.Provider`/`*.Consumer` member expression.

title: React Compiler ordering guarantee only holds when the compiler comes from a preset; a compiler listed in `plugins` runs before v6y and drops JSX-comment ignores
claim: The comment claims v6y's Program.enter runs first because plugins run before presets, but Metro adds v6y through the programmatic `plugins` option, which Babel merges after the config file's `plugins`; a user who lists `babel-plugin-react-compiler` in babel.config.js `plugins` (the setup React's docs give for non-Expo apps) gets the compiler's Program.enter first.
evidence: packages/metro/src/transformer.ts:43 appends the plugin to `args.plugins` (programmatic); babel-plugin test 'survives plugins that drop JSX comments' only covers the preset case; README.md:244 reports verification with Expo's template, where the compiler is inside babel-preset-expo. Babel's config-file-before-programmatic merge order is from knowledge, not reproduced.
impact: Bare RN apps with the compiler in `plugins` lose `{/* v6y-ignore */}` suppressions silently (the `//` statement-level form still works).
fix: Either document 'put `v6y/babel` first in `plugins` when you list the React Compiler yourself', or make the Metro transformer extract ignore comments from the raw `src` text (it has it) and pass them to the plugin as an option, independent of plugin order.

title: CI never type-checks a consumer of the published `.d.ts`, and unit tests run only on React 18
claim: The example job runs `npx jest` but never `tsc`, so the example's `"types": ["jest","node","v6y/jest"]` (examples/expo-app/tsconfig.json) and its `v6y/metro`/`v6y` imports are never compiled against the shipped declarations; the root test job uses `react 18.3.1`/`react-test-renderer 18.3.1` (package.json devDependencies) while `peerDependencies.react` is `>=18` and the example and field targets are React 19.3.
evidence: ci.yml has no tsc/`--noEmit` step; root package.json devDependencies pin React 18.3.1; examples/expo-app/package.json uses react 19.3.0 and typescript ~6.0.3.
impact: A broken or incompatible declaration file (e.g. the global `jest` augmentation under TS 6) or a React 19 fiber-shape regression in collect.ts would ship unnoticed except through the Jest showcase.
fix: Add `npx tsc --noEmit -p examples/expo-app` (or `npx @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack packages/v6y`) to the example job, and run the react-native package tests under React 19 as well (a second vitest invocation with an alias, or move the devDependency to 19).

title: `v6y/jest` types target Jest only; Vitest users get a type error and no auto-registration
claim: The global augmentation declares only `jest.Matchers`, and matchers register only when `globalThis.expect` exists, although the README (line 227) and the file header advertise Vitest support.
evidence: jest.ts:143-151 `declare global { namespace jest { interface Matchers<R> … } }`; jest.ts:154-155 `globalExpect?.extend`; no `declare module 'vitest'` anywhere in packages/react-native/src.
impact: In Vitest, `expect(x).toBeAccessible()` is a TS error and does nothing unless `globals: true` and the user calls `expect.extend(matchers)`.
fix: Add `declare module 'vitest' { interface Assertion<T> { toBeAccessible(options?: AccessibleOptions): Promise<T> } }`, and document `import { matchers } from 'v6y/jest'; expect.extend(matchers)` for Vitest.

title: No `engines` field although the CLI needs Node ≥18 and TypeScript configs need Node ≥22.18
claim: The package declares no `engines`, so npm never warns users on unsupported Node versions; the sources use nothing newer than Node 18 (fetch is not used in the CLI; no `findLast`/`structuredClone`/`globSync`), and the 22.18 requirement for `.ts` configs is only surfaced at runtime (cli/src/index.ts:59).
evidence: grep across packages/*/src for post-Node-18 APIs found none; `loadConfig` error message at cli/src/index.ts:59 mentions 22.18; README.md:131 documents it.
impact: Users on old Node get confusing failures instead of an install-time warning.
fix: Add `"engines": { "node": ">=18" }` to packages/v6y/package.json (and the root), keep the 22.18 runtime message.

title: README shipped to npm is stale in places and uses repo-relative links
claim: The root README is copied verbatim into the package (bundle.mjs:82): line 228 lists the CLI as `init`, `rules`, `check` and `dev` (no `fix`, `mcp`); line 258 still lists 'a single `v6y` npm package' under Next up although commit cd102a4 shipped it; line 247 says the runtime on a real device is not yet verified while commit 86e9c23's message records an Android/Expo Go run; lines 18, 107 and 166 link `./examples/expo-app`, `./docs/agents.md`, `./docs/rules/README.md` relative to the repo, which the npm page may not resolve.
evidence: Read README.md lines 18, 107, 166, 228, 247, 258; `git log --format=%B 86e9c23` ('Device (Android, Expo Go, new architecture): …'); bundle.mjs:81-82 copies the root README; `git log --oneline` shows cd102a4 'Ship as one package'.
impact: The first thing npm visitors read contradicts the product's own state and may show dead links.
fix: Update the Status section and the command table, remove the done item, and use absolute GitHub URLs for the three links (or a short npm-specific README).

title: Composite Action exposes no outputs or step summary and shells out through `npx` after already locating the binary
claim: The Action has no `outputs:` (issue count, failed) and writes nothing to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so workflows cannot branch on the result or show it on the run page; the script verifies `node_modules/.bin/v6y` exists and then runs `npx --no-install v6y`, an npm-7-era alias.
evidence: action.yml has `inputs` and `runs` only; run script lines 30-41; `npx --no-install v6y help` still works on npm 11.12.1 (exit 0).
impact: Users wanting a comment bot, a gate on warnings, or a summary must re-run the CLI themselves.
fix: Run `node_modules/.bin/v6y check … --format github` and also `--format json` into a file, set `outputs.issues`/`outputs.failed` via `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, and append a short table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

title: AppRegistry wrapper also wraps the LogBox root: it hijacks rootOwner and kills auto-capture once dismissed
claim: `setWrapperComponentProvider(() => V6yProvider)` ignores the `appKey` argument, so when the LogBox inspector opens (any red-box error, or tapping v6y's own warning banner) a second V6yProvider mounts in the LogBox root, steals `rootOwner`, starts a second poll loop that captures the LogBox UI as screen "App", and on dismiss sets `rootOwner = undefined`, after which the app's poll loop returns early forever and manual `capture()` warns that no provider is mounted.
evidence: RN 0.88 AppRegistryImpl.js:92-111 passes `wrapperComponentProvider(appParameters, appKey)` for every app key and sets `isLogBox: appKey === 'LogBox'` right after; AppRegistry.js:15 registers 'LogBox' via `registerComponent`; AppContainer-dev.js:167-171 renders `<WrapperComponent initialProps>` regardless of isLogBox. index.tsx:95 `rootOwner = this`, :102 `if (rootOwner === this) rootOwner = undefined`, :109-115 `check()` returns on `!root` and falls back to 'App' after 3 polls without a route. iOS RCTLogBox.mm:75-76 `setHidden:YES; _view = nil` destroys the LogBox surface on hide (unmount path). Android path not read.
impact: In a routine dev session (one red box, or tapping the banner v6y itself produces) in-app auditing silently stops for the rest of the session and a bogus 'App' snapshot of RN's LogBox UI is sent to Metro and saved to .v6y/snapshots.
fix: Return no wrapper for LogBox: `setWrapperComponentProvider((_, appKey) => (appKey === 'LogBox' ? null : V6yProvider))` (AppContainer checks `WrapperComponent != null`). Also keep a set of mounted providers instead of a single `rootOwner`, never let a later root displace an earlier mounted one, and don't reset ownership on unmount while another provider is mounted.

title: Jest matcher audits the entire tree when given a ReactTestInstance (e.g. RNTL getByTestId result)
claim: `fiberOf()` accepts any object with `_fiber` (including an element instance from `screen.getByRole()` / `findByProps()`), and `auditRendered` then calls `collect(findCurrentRoot(fiber))`, so the assertion silently audits every element in the rendered tree instead of the one passed.
evidence: jest.ts:52-54 candidates include `received` itself; jest.ts:92 `collect(findCurrentRoot(fiber), ...)` walks up to the HostRoot. Reproduced with /tmp/claude-60452/-var-home-matthew/177dfed2-8525-4556-89f6-1dd8b44cbebe/scratchpad/probe-instance.cjs: passing the labelled 'good' button instance returned `missing-label`/`missing-role` on node 3, the unrelated sibling.
impact: `await expect(getByTestId('card')).toBeAccessible()` passes or fails because of unrelated elements; users believe they scoped the check and get misleading results.
fix: When `received._fiber` is not the root instance, collect from that fiber (make `collect` accept a start fiber and include it, walking `return` to inherit hidden/modal/ancestor context), or reject element instances with an explicit error naming the supported inputs.

title: Hidden Offscreen subtrees (suspended Suspense content, <Activity mode="hidden">) are collected as visible
claim: Fibers with tags other than host/composite (including OffscreenComponent, tag 22) fall through to `walk(f.child, parent, next)`, so the primary children of a Suspense boundary that is currently showing its fallback, and `<Activity mode="hidden">` content, are emitted as visible nodes next to the fallback even though React hides their native views.
evidence: Reproduced with /tmp/claude-60452/-var-home-matthew/177dfed2-8525-4556-89f6-1dd8b44cbebe/scratchpad/probe-suspense.cjs (react-test-renderer 18.3.1 concurrent root): while `toJSON()` shows only 'Loading…', `collect()` returns the hidden 'Primary button' node plus the fallback. probe-offscreen.cjs shows the hidden marker is `memoizedState !== null` on the tag-22 fiber (memoizedProps.mode stays 'visible' on bail-out). React 19.3 renderer (ReactFabric-dev.js:8162-8245) sets `memoizedState = {baseLanes, cachePool}` when hidden and `null` when visible, same marker. On Paper (legacy roots) a boundary suspended at mount commits its partial primary tree hidden, so this also hits first loads there.
impact: Wrong results during loading/transition captures (Relay/TanStack suspense refetches, React 19 Activity, Expo Router 58 NavigationAwareActivity): duplicate-label and other rules see both the fallback and the natively hidden content; nested-interactive/contrast run on invisible elements.
fix: In `visit`, skip hidden offscreen trees: `if (tag === 22 /* OffscreenComponent */ && f.memoizedState !== null) return;` (covers Suspense fallback state and Activity hidden mode in React 18 and 19), and add a test with a concurrent root that suspends after mount.

title: Auto-capture keys on route name only: same screen with new params (and non-route UI changes) is never re-captured
claim: `check()` and `trackNavigation` compare only the focused route name to `lastScreen`, so pushing the same route with different params (Product 1 -> Product 2), opening an RN `<Modal>`, a bottom sheet, a menu, or data arriving after `delayMs` never triggers a capture; the README's modal isolation is only reachable through a manual `capture()` or a navigation-based modal.
evidence: index.tsx:111-118 (`route ?? 'App'`, `if (name === lastScreen) return;`) and :200-204 (`getCurrentRoute()?.name`, same comparison). `focusedRouteName` (collect.ts:229-258) returns `route.name` only; RN `Modal` is not a navigation route so the name does not change when one opens.
impact: Large classes of screens (detail pages reached repeatedly, dialogs, sheets, lazily loaded content) are audited once or never; users assume navigation coverage they don't have.
fix: Have `focusedRouteName` return `{ name, key }` and dedupe on `route.key` (unique per route instance); additionally compute a cheap tree signature per poll (focused key + number of visible modal/`aria-modal` hosts + host count) and re-capture, debounced by `delayMs`, when it changes.

title: Screen names are leaf route names, so Expo Router/nested navigators collide and overwrite each other's snapshots
claim: `focusedRouteName` reports the deepest focused `route.name`, which in Expo Router is the segment relative to the nearest layout (e.g. `index`, `[id]`), so two tabs each with their own stack and an `index.tsx` both report screen `index`; `handleReport` saves to `.v6y/snapshots/<screen>.<platform>.json`, so the later capture overwrites the earlier one and `screens.ignore` cannot target one of them.
evidence: collect.ts:235-252 uses `p.route.name`; packages/cli/src/index.ts `handleReport` builds the file name from `snapshot.screen` only; Expo Router 58 vendored core (expo-router/build/react-navigation/core/useDescriptors.js:143-146) passes the per-navigator route to SceneView; example app layouts show names like `(tabs)`, `menu`, `product/[id]` which are only unique because no nested `_layout` repeats a leaf.
impact: Silent data loss in snapshot files and CI `--changed` coverage, plus ambiguous terminal output (`v6y · index`).
fix: Accumulate the focused chain of route names while walking (e.g. `(tabs)/home/index`) or use Expo Router's pathname when available, and use that for `screen`; keep the leaf name for display if desired.

title: Jest matcher loads v6y.config via require(), which fails for the .mjs/.mts/ESM configs the README advertises
claim: `loadProjectConfig` resolves any of `CONFIG_FILES` (including `v6y.config.mts`/`.mjs`) and loads non-JSON files with `require(file)`; Jest's runtime refuses to `require` ESM files, so an `.mjs` config (or a `.js` config in a `"type": "module"` project) throws inside the matcher on Node < 24.9.
evidence: jest.ts:44-47; packages/cli/src/index.ts CONFIG_FILES includes `v6y.config.mts` and `v6y.config.mjs`; README says ".js, .mjs, .cjs and .json work too"; jest-runtime 30 (examples/expo-app/node_modules/jest-runtime/build/index.js:452) throws "Must use import to load ES Module ... Use Node v24.9+ where Jest supports require(esm) natively". Not reproduced (this machine runs Node 24.15, where require(esm) works).
impact: `toBeAccessible()` fails with an unrelated-looking ESM error for users who followed the README's config-format claim.
fix: In the Jest path support `.ts/.js/.cjs/.json` only and throw a clear error for `.mjs/.mts` ("use v6y.config.ts or .cjs in Jest"), or catch the ESM error and explain it; document the limitation in the README's config section.

title: react-native-gesture-handler Pressable/Touchables (and GestureDetector taps) are invisible to the collector
claim: `isInteractive` only recognises `onResponderRelease`/`onPress` on the host, but RNGH's `Pressable` strips `onPress` and renders `RNGestureHandlerButton` with `testOnly_onPress` (tests only), and RNGH's TouchableOpacity/Highlight (GenericTouchable) put only gesture props on the button host and the a11y props on an inner Animated.View, so none of these controls are marked interactive; `RectButton`/`BorderlessButton` are detected only by accident because `{...rest}` forwards `onPress` to the host.
evidence: RNGH 3.3.0 src/components/Pressable/Pressable.tsx:57-59 (destructures onPress) and :386-411 (`NativeButton {...remainingProps} testOnly_onPress={IS_TEST_ENV ? onPress : undefined}`); src/components/touchables/GenericTouchable.tsx:248-266 (host gets onHandlerStateChange/onGestureEvent only; coreProps with accessibilityLabel/Role go to Animated.View); GestureButtons.tsx:136-150 + createNativeWrapper.tsx:36-82 (onPress lands in childProps -> host). GestureDetector attaches by view tag (GestureDetector/index.tsx:143-176), no host prop at all.
impact: missing-label, missing-role, nested-interactive, duplicate-label and touch-target-size never run on these buttons (false negatives), and an RNGH button wrapping an RN Pressable is not reported as nested-interactive. Apps on RNGH-based design systems get a clean bill of health they didn't earn.
fix: Treat `RNGestureHandlerButton` hosts (unless `enabled === false`) as interactive, honour `testOnly_onPress`, add a `hostTypes.interactive` (and `scroll`) config so apps can declare custom native controls, and document that `GestureDetector`-only taps cannot be detected.

title: v6y's console.warn creates a LogBox banner that the next captures audit, because collect() walks from the HostRoot rather than the provider
claim: The per-capture summary is logged with `console.warn`, which LogBox intercepts into a persistent on-screen notification; that banner is rendered inside the same React root as a sibling of the wrapper component, and `capture()` collects from the HostRoot (index.tsx:138), so from the second capture on every screen snapshot contains LogBox's own Pressables (no role/label) and text, reported with no source.
evidence: RN 0.88 LogBox.js:109-117 replaces console.warn with registerWarning; AppContainer-dev.js:167-171 wraps `innerView` in WrapperComponent and ~:208 renders `<LogBoxNotificationContainer />` as a sibling inside the root View; LogBoxNotification.js:41-59 and LogBoxButton.js:58-82 are `Pressable`s with no accessibilityRole or label (dismiss button is a glyph) so `missing-role` (warning in recommended) fires; `currentRoot()` (index.tsx:74-77) returns the HostRoot via `findCurrentRoot`. Not run on device.
impact: Self-inflicted noise on every screen after the first finding (plus a yellow banner per screen the developer must dismiss), and it is the gateway to the LogBox-root hijack finding.
fix: Log the summary with `console.log` (or `LogBox.ignoreLogs([/^\[v6y\]/])`), and collect from the provider's own current fiber: from `findCurrentRoot(...)` descend to the fiber whose `stateNode === rootOwner` and walk its children. That also excludes RN's DebuggingOverlay/Inspector and Expo dev overlays.

title: Reanimated animated styles are snapshotted at their first-render values
claim: The collector reads `memoizedProps.style`, but Reanimated replaces `useAnimatedStyle` handles with the values captured on the component's first render and never updates them, and RN Animated passes the JS-side values from the last React render, so colors/opacity driven by animations (interpolateColor tab labels, pressed states, fades) are stale in snapshots.
evidence: react-native-reanimated 4.7.1 src/createAnimatedComponent/PropsFilter.tsx:28-60 (`_initialPropsMap.set(handle, {...initial.value, ...initialUpdaterRun(updater)})` only when `_isFirstRender`, reused afterwards); RN Animated createAnimatedComponent.js:126-152 spreads `reducedProps` from `useAnimatedProps`. pickStyle (collect.ts:91-100) feeds these into `text-contrast`.
impact: text-contrast computed from wrong colors on animated text/backgrounds (false positives and negatives); animated visibility cannot be inferred.
fix: Document the limitation; for Reanimated, read `style.initial.value` only as a last resort and mark nodes whose style contains animated handles (`viewDescriptors`) so contrast is skipped rather than guessed, mirroring the 'don't guess' policy for unknown colors.

title: react-test-renderer is required at call time but not declared as a (peer) dependency
claim: `renderElement` does `require('react-test-renderer')` when `toBeAccessible` receives a React element, but neither `@v6y/react-native` nor the `v6y` bundle lists it, so projects without it get a bare 'Cannot find module' error.
evidence: jest.ts:58; packages/react-native/package.json peerDependencies list only react/react-native; packages/v6y/package.json likewise. RNTL 13.3.3 still peers on `react-test-renderer >=18.2.0` and exposes `UNSAFE_root = renderer.root` (fetched build/render.js), so RNTL users usually have it, but element-only users may not.
impact: Confusing failure for the README's `await expect(<Checkout />).toBeAccessible()` form in projects without RNTL.
fix: Declare `react-test-renderer` as an optional peerDependency and wrap the require in a try/catch that explains how to install it (or render through RNTL when present).

title: isWeb() sniffs `document`, so a jsdom Jest environment turns onClick-only wrapper Views back into pressables
claim: `isWeb()` returns true whenever `document` and `window` exist; under `testEnvironment: 'jsdom'` (projects that also test web code, or jest-expo/web) native-platform snapshots count `onClick`-only Views as interactive, reintroducing the EventStopper false-positive class the field test removed.
evidence: collect.ts:131-143; the field reports (REPORT.md item 1) show this class was ~50% of false positives. Both @react-native/jest-preset (jest-preset.js:40) and jest-expo native presets (jest-preset.js:30) use node-style environments, so it only triggers when users opt into jsdom. Not reproduced.
impact: Precision regression in a common Jest configuration, with no hint in the output as to why.
fix: Pass the platform into `collect` (from `Platform.OS` / `options.platform`) and use `platform === 'web'` instead of DOM sniffing.

title: Snapshot fields collected but never read: hint, style.opacity, window/fontScale
claim: The collector records `hint` (collect.ts:304), `style.opacity` (collect.ts:98) and `window.{width,height,fontScale}` (index.tsx:146), but no rule, the engine or the CLI reads any of them.
evidence: grep over packages/core/src and packages/cli/src for `.hint`, `.window`, `.fontScale` returns zero uses; `opacity` appears only in types.ts.
impact: Dead schema surface that suggests capabilities (font-scale checks, opacity-aware hiding/contrast, hint-aware labelling) that don't exist; adds snapshot size and maintenance.
fix: Either consume them (e.g. treat `opacity: 0` as hidden, factor opacity into contrast, use fontScale for a 200% check) or drop them from A11yNode/ScreenSnapshot until a rule needs them.

title: AppContainer's `initialProps` is treated as runtime options
claim: When installed via AppRegistry, the wrapper receives `initialProps`, so `Object.keys(options).length` is always >= 1 and `configure(projectConfig, { initialProps })` runs on every root mount (including LogBox's), storing an unknown `runtime.initialProps` key.
evidence: RN 0.88 AppContainer-dev.js:167-171 renders `<WrapperComponent initialProps={initialProps}>`; index.tsx:93-94 destructures only `children`/`config` and spreads the rest into `options`.
impact: Harmless today (config re-resolution and a stray key), but it defeats the 'only configure when the user passed options' intent and will bite as soon as runtime options get validated.
fix: Pick known RuntimeOptions keys explicitly (enabled, endpoint, log, autoCapture, report, collect) instead of spreading `...options`.

title: Manual `import 'v6y/auto'` / <V6yProvider> ships the collector and rules engine into production and installs the AppRegistry wrapper there
claim: auto.ts has no `__DEV__` guard: it requires `./index` (which imports all of `@v6y/core`), `v6y/project-config` and `react-native`, and calls `setWrapperComponentProvider` unconditionally, so the README's documented non-Metro path (`import 'v6y/auto'` at the top of the entry file) bundles ~340 KB of dev-only code into release builds and overrides any other wrapper provider in production; only the withV6y injection is dev-only.
evidence: auto.ts:12-20; index.tsx:2 top-level import of @v6y/core; dist sizes: packages/core/dist 240K, packages/react-native/dist 100K; metro/src/transformer.ts:33 injects the import only when `options.dev`; README 'Production bundles are untouched'.
impact: Bundle bloat and a wrapper component in production for the non-Metro setup the README recommends; contradicts the README's promise for that path.
fix: Wrap auto.ts's body in `if (__DEV__) { ... }` (Metro's constant folding drops the requires) and lazy-require `@v6y/core` inside `capture()`/`configure()` so a manual <V6yProvider> in production carries only the tiny class.

title: TextInput hosts are classified as pressable controls
claim: RN's TextInput spreads Pressability handlers (incl. `onResponderRelease`) onto its host, so every text field gets `interactive: true` and is treated like a button by rules that don't special-case inputs.
evidence: RN 0.88 TextInput.js:519 (`usePressability`), :588 and :659 (`{...eventHandlers}` on the host); collect.ts:141 marks any `onResponderRelease` host interactive. Rule consequences traced: duplicate-label groups a 'Search' field with a 'Search' button; nested-interactive flags an input inside a tappable row; touch-target-size measures inputs. missing-label/missing-role are shielded by `hasIntrinsicRole`.
impact: Occasional false positives (duplicate-label, nested-interactive) on forms, and 'interactive' no longer means 'pressable control' for rule authors.
fix: Don't set `interactive` for `kind === 'input'` (and other intrinsic-role hosts), or add a distinct `control` flag; conversely consider marking Switch/Slider hosts as controls so unlabeled switches can be reported.

title: Recorded Jest snapshots collide across test files
claim: With V6Y_SNAPSHOTS set, each assertion is saved as `<sanitised currentTestName>.<platform>.json`, so two tests with the same name in different files (common: 'renders correctly') overwrite each other.
evidence: jest.ts:112-118 builds the name from `snapshot.screen` only, which defaults to `this.currentTestName` (jest.ts:122).
impact: CI `v6y check --changed` sees only the last writer, reporting missing coverage or stale snapshots for the overwritten screen.
fix: Include `this.testPath` (relative) or a short hash of it in the file name, and warn when overwriting a file written in the same run.
